Others said: they are the sons of a man's wife by another husband.

Those who said so:

• Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding his words ﴿and has made for you from your spouses sons and ḥafadah﴾, he says: the sons of a man's wife who are not from him. It is said: al-ḥafadah: a man who works before a man; one says: so-and-so ḥafada for us (serves us). Some men claim that al-ḥafadah are the in-laws [[al-akhtan: plural of khatn, with a sukun on the ta', meaning the husband of a man's daughter.]] of a man.

The correct position in this matter, in my view, is to say: Allah, exalted is He, informed His servants, reminding them of His favour upon them in what He made for them of spouses and sons. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has made for you from yourselves spouses, and has made for you from your spouses sons and ḥafadah﴾. So He informed them that He made for them from their spouses sons and ḥafadah. In the speech of the Arabs, ḥafadah is the plural of ḥafid, just as kadhbah is the plural of kadhib and fasaqah the plural of fasiq. The ḥafid in their speech is one who is light in service and work. Al-ḥafd is lightness in work; it is said: the camel passed, yaḥfidu ḥafadanan, when it passed hastening in its course. From this is their saying: "ilayka nas'a wa-nahfid", meaning we hasten to work by Your obedience. From it one says: ḥafada lahu yaḥfudu ḥafdan, ḥafudan and ḥafadanan. From it is the saying of al-Ra'i:

kallaftu majhūlahā nūqan yamāniyyatan ... idhā al-ḥudātu 'alā akṣā'ihā ḥafadū [[al-aksa': singular kasa, on the pattern qifl, the hinder part of the rump or the hinder part of anything; plural aksa'. Lisan al-'Arab (k-s-a). Abu 'Ubaydah recited: "kallaftu majhūlahā..." ... "idhā al-ḥaddād..." ... "ḥafadū". The word al-ḥaddād in al-Azhari's transmission is probably a corruption of al-ḥudāh.]]

Since the meaning of ḥafadah is what we have mentioned, that they are those who hasten in serving a man and are light in it, and since Allah, dhikruhu, informed us that among the favours He bestowed upon us is that He made for us ḥafadah who serve us, and our children, our spouses who are fit for service, whether from us or from others, and our in-laws who are the husbands of our daughters from our spouses, and our servants from our slaves, if they serve us, they deserve the name ḥafadah. Allah, exalted is He, did not indicate by the apparent sense of His revelation, nor by the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, nor by any rational proof, that He meant one type of ḥafadah to the exclusion of another; and since He had bestowed all of these upon us, it is not for us to restrict it to a particular kind of ḥafadah rather than a general one, except what the community has agreed does not fall within them. Given this, each of the sayings we have mentioned from those we named has a valid aspect and a line of interpretation. Yet the most correct of these sayings is what we have chosen, for the proof we have shown.

* *

And His words ﴿and provided for you of the good things﴾

He says: and provided you with lawful livelihood, sustenance and food. ﴿Then in falsehood do they believe﴾: He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: those allies of Satan who prohibit for them the baḥā'ir, the sawā'ib and the wasā'il; so do these polytheists believe in falsehood ﴿and in the favour of Allah do they disbelieve﴾: He says: and in what Allah has made lawful for them of that, and bestowed upon them by making it lawful, they disbelieve; that is, they deny its lawfulness, and deny that Allah made it lawful.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 73–74:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens and the earth at all, and they are not able [to do anything]﴾ [16:73] ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [16:74].

Exalted is His remembrance says: These polytheists worship, besides Allah, idols that do not possess for them any provision from the heavens, because they are not able to send down rain from them to revive the dead lands. And [they possess no provision] from the earth, since it is not able to bring forth for them any of its plants and fruits, nor any of the other things which He, exalted is He, enumerated in this verse as bounties He bestowed upon them. ﴿And they are not able﴾: meaning, their idols do not possess anything of the heavens and the earth; rather, they and everything in the heavens and the earth belong to Allah's dominion. ﴿And they are not able﴾: meaning, they are not capable of anything.

* *

And His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾

Meaning: do not liken Allah to examples, and do not ascribe to Him similitudes, for He has no like and no equal.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "al-amthal" means the likenesses.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾: it means their taking of idols. He says: Do not set up for Me another god besides Me, for there is no god but Me.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens and the earth at all, and they are not able﴾: he said: These are the idols worshipped besides Allah; they possess for those who worship them no provision, no harm, no benefit, and no life or resurrection.

* *

And His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾

Indeed, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾: He says: and Allah, O people, knows the error and the correctness of the examples you make and strike, and all other things; and you do not know the correctness of that from its error.

The grammarians differed concerning what governs the word ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ (shay'an, "anything"). Some of the Basran grammarians said: it is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for "provision" (rizq), and its meaning is: they do not possess a little provision nor a great deal. Some of the Kufan grammarians said: ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ is in the accusative because "provision" falls upon it, as the Exalted said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?﴾ [77:25–26], meaning, it gathers the living and the dead. A similar example is His words, exalted is He: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger, an orphan of near relationship, or a needy person in misery﴾ [90:14–16]. He said: And if "provision" were with the thing, its genitive case would be permissible: "they do not possess the provision of anything from the heavens." Similar is His words ﴿then the recompense is like what he killed of livestock﴾ [5:95].

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 73–74:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens and the earth at all, and they are not able [to do anything]﴾ [16:73] ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾ [16:74].

Exalted is His remembrance says: These polytheists worship, besides Allah, idols that do not possess for them any provision from the heavens, because they are not able to send down rain from them to revive the dead lands. And [they possess no provision] from the earth, since it is not able to bring forth for them any of its plants and fruits, nor any of the other things which He, exalted is He, enumerated in this verse as bounties He bestowed upon them. ﴿And they are not able﴾: meaning, their idols do not possess anything of the heavens and the earth; rather, they and everything in the heavens and the earth belong to Allah's dominion. ﴿And they are not able﴾: meaning, they are not capable of anything.

* *

And His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾

Meaning: do not liken Allah to examples, and do not ascribe to Him similitudes, for He has no like and no equal.

The people of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "al-amthal" means the likenesses.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾: it means their taking of idols. He says: Do not set up for Me another god besides Me, for there is no god but Me.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which possesses no provision for them from the heavens and the earth at all, and they are not able﴾: he said: These are the idols worshipped besides Allah; they possess for those who worship them no provision, no harm, no benefit, and no life or resurrection.

* *

And His words ﴿So do not strike examples for Allah﴾

Indeed, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge, who neither begets nor is begotten, and to whom no one is equal. ﴿Indeed, Allah knows, and you do not know﴾: He says: and Allah, O people, knows the error and the correctness of the examples you make and strike, and all other things; and you do not know the correctness of that from its error.

The grammarians differed concerning what governs the word ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ (shay'an, "anything"). Some of the Basran grammarians said: it is in the accusative as a substitute (badal) for "provision" (rizq), and its meaning is: they do not possess a little provision nor a great deal. Some of the Kufan grammarians said: ﴿شَيْئًا﴾ is in the accusative because "provision" falls upon it, as the Exalted said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a receptacle, for the living and the dead?﴾ [77:25–26], meaning, it gathers the living and the dead. A similar example is His words, exalted is He: ﴿or feeding on a day of hunger, an orphan of near relationship, or a needy person in misery﴾ [90:14–16]. He said: And if "provision" were with the thing, its genitive case would be permissible: "they do not possess the provision of anything from the heavens." Similar is His words ﴿then the recompense is like what he killed of livestock﴾ [5:95].

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 16, verse 75:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, having no power over anything; and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so that he spends of it secretly and openly. Are they equal? Praise belongs to God. But most of them do not know.﴾

His, the Exalted's, words mean: And He makes for you, O people, a comparison between the disbelievers among His servants and the believers among them. As for the likeness of the disbeliever, he does not act in obedience to God, nor does he do any good, nor does he spend his wealth in any cause of God, because the abandonment of God has overcome him; he is like the owned slave who has no power over anything to spend. As for the believer in God, he acts in obedience to God and spends his wealth in His cause; he is like the free man to whom God has given wealth, so that he spends of it secretly and openly, meaning: with the knowledge of people and without their knowledge. ﴿Are they equal?﴾ meaning: Are equal the slave who owns nothing and has no power over it, and this free man whom God has provided with goodly provision, so that he spends as described? Likewise, the disbeliever who practises the disobedience of God and opposes His command is not equal to the believer who practises His obedience.

Some of the people of knowledge have said in agreement with what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, having no power over anything﴾: This is a parable God struck for the disbeliever, who was given wealth but did not send forward any good in it and did not act in it by obedience to God. God, the Exalted, said ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us﴾: this is the believer, whom God gave wealth, and he acted in it by obedience to God and took up gratitude and recognition of God's right, so God rewarded him for the provision He gave him with the lasting, enduring provision for its people in Paradise. God, the Exalted, said ﴿Are they equal as a parable?﴾ By God, they are not equal. ﴿Praise belongs to God; but most of them do not know.﴾

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿a slave owned, having no power over anything﴾: He said: this is the disbeliever who does not act in obedience to God and does not spend anything good. ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us﴾: He said: this is the believer who obeys God with his self and his wealth.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿God strikes a parable: a slave owned, having no power over anything﴾: meaning the disbeliever, that he cannot manage to spend any expenditure in the cause of God. ﴿and one whom We have provided with goodly provision from Us, so that he spends of it secretly and openly﴾: meaning the believer. This parable concerns spending.

* *

As for His words ﴿Praise belongs to God﴾:

It means: complete praise belongs to God alone, exclusively, apart from what you, O people, worship besides Him of idols; so praise Him alone, not them.

* *

As for His words ﴿But most of them do not know﴾:

It means: The matter is not as you do, nor is the saying as you say. The idols have no hand or favour with them that would merit praise; rather, praise belongs to God. But most of these unbelievers who worship them do not know that this is so, and so, through their ignorance of what they do and leave undone, they make them partners with God in worship and praise.

Mujahid used to say: God struck this parable, and the other parable after it, for Himself and for the gods that are worshipped besides Him.

The commentary on the words of God Most High: "And Allah strikes a parable: two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything, and he is a burden upon his master; wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who enjoins justice while he is on a straight path?" (16:76)

This is a parable which God struck for Himself and the idols that are worshipped besides Him. God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "Allah strikes a parable: two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything." He means by this the idol, that it does not hear anything nor speaks, for it is either carved wood or manufactured brass, unable to benefit those who serve it or to ward off harm from it. "And he is a burden upon his master" means: he is a dependent upon his cousin, his allies and the people of his guardianship. Likewise the idol is a burden upon those who worship it; it needs to be carried, placed and served, like the dumb man among people who is unable to do anything, so he is a burden upon his guardians among his paternal cousins and others. "Wherever he directs him, he brings no good" means: wherever he directs him, he brings no good, because he does not understand what is said to him, and cannot express what he wants, so he does not understand and is not understood. Likewise the idol does not comprehend what is said to it, so it does not obey any command given to it, nor does it speak to command or forbid. God Most High says: "Is he equal to one who enjoins justice?" meaning: is this dumb one, a burden upon his master, who brings no good wherever he is directed, equal to one who speaks and talks, who enjoins the truth and calls to it, and that is Allah, the One, the Subduer, who calls His servants to His oneness and obedience? He means: He, may His remembrance be exalted, is not equal to the idol whose description is what has been described.

* *

As for His words: "And he is upon a straight path."

He means: while he enjoins justice, he is upon a path of truth in calling to justice, and his command to it is upright, not deviating from the truth nor departing from it.

The interpreters differed concerning the one for whom this parable was struck. Some of them said in this regard something similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, concerning "unable to do anything": he said, it is the idol. "Is he equal to one who enjoins justice?": he said, Allah enjoins justice. "And he is upon a straight path." And Mujahid used to say likewise, except that he used to say: the first parable too was struck by Allah for Himself and for the idol.

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God, may His remembrance be exalted: "a slave owned, who has no power over anything, and one whom We have provided with a goodly provision from Us" and "two men, one of them dumb" and "and who enjoins justice": he said, all of this is a parable of the God of truth and what is called upon besides Him, of falsehood.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, concerning "And Allah strikes a parable: two men, one of them dumb": he said, this is only a parable which Allah struck.

Others said: rather, both parables are for the believer and the disbeliever. This is a saying narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and we have mentioned the narration from him regarding the first parable in its place.

As for the other parable:

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And Allah strikes a parable: two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything, and he is a burden upon his master" ... to the end of the verse. He means by the dumb one: the one who is a burden upon his master, the disbeliever; and by His words "and who enjoins justice": the believer. This parable concerns deeds.

Al-Hasan ibn al-Sabah al-Bazzar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Ishaq al-Silhini narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from Ibrahim, from 'Ikrimah, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: "Allah strikes a parable: a slave owned" he said: it was revealed concerning a man of Quraysh and his slave. And concerning His words "two men, one of them dumb, unable to do anything" ... to His words "and he is upon a straight path," he said: he is 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. He said: And the dumb one, who wherever he is directed brings no good, that is the client of 'Uthman ibn 'Affan. 'Uthman used to spend on him, support him and provide for his needs, and the other one hated Islam and rejected it, and forbade him from charity and goodness, so they were revealed concerning the two of them.

We have chosen the view we have chosen regarding the first parable because He, may His remembrance be exalted, struck the likeness of the disbeliever with the slave whose description He gave, and struck the likeness of the believer with the one to whom He gave a goodly provision, so he spends from what He has provided him, secretly and openly. It was not permissible for that to be a parable of God, since God only likened the disbeliever who has no power over anything to one whom He has not provided with a provision from which he may spend secretly; and He likened the believer whom God has enabled to obey Him and guided to his rectitude, so he acts by what pleases God, to the free man to whom provision has been extended, so that he spends from it secretly and openly. God, may His remembrance be exalted, is the Provider, not the provided, so it is not permissible that His bounty and generosity be likened to the spending of one who is provided with goodly provision. As for the second parable, it is a likening by Him, may His remembrance be exalted, of one likened to the dumb one who has no power over anything, and the disbelievers—there is no doubt that among them are those who have much wealth, and who at times cause great harm through their corruption—so it is not fitting that they be described as having no power over anything, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, said as a parable for one who has power over many things. If that is so, the most fitting meaning of it is the likening of what has no power over anything, as God, may His remembrance be exalted, likened by it what has no power over anything, namely the idol which has no power over anything, to the dumb one who has no power over anything, a burden upon his master, as He said and described.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth. And the matter of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or it is nearer﴾ [16:77]

His saying, may He be remembered: To Allah, O people, belongs the dominion over what is hidden from your sight in the heavens and the earth, apart from your gods which you invoke besides Him, and apart from everything other than Him; none other than Him possesses that. ﴿And the matter of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye﴾ means: the matter of the establishment of the Resurrection and the Hour, in which creation will be raised to stand at the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection, is nothing but like a glance of the eye, because that is only that it be said to it, "Be," and it is.

As related:

* Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿but as a glance of the eye or it is nearer﴾: "And the Hour is like the glance of the eye, or nearer."

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And the matter of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye﴾, he said: "It is that He says, 'Be,' and it is, like the glance of the eye. So the matter of the Hour is like the glance of the eye or nearer," meaning: He says, "or it is nearer than the glance of the eye."

* * *

And His saying, ﴿Indeed, Allah is over all things competent﴾

He says: Indeed Allah is capable of establishing the Hour in a time nearer than the glance of the eye, and capable of whatever He wills of all things; nothing He intends is beyond His power.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing, and He made for you hearing, sight, and hearts, that perhaps you might give thanks﴾ (78)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Allah, exalted is He, taught you what you did not know after He brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, when you did not understand anything nor know anything. He provided you with minds by which you comprehend and distinguish good from evil, and He gave you sight by which you see what you did not see. He made for you hearing, by which you hear voices, so that some of you understand from others what you converse about among yourselves; and sight, by which you see persons and thereby recognize one another and distinguish some from others. ﴿And the hearts﴾ means: and the hearts by which you recognize things, so that you retain them, and reflect, so that you understand by them. ﴿That perhaps you might give thanks﴾ means: We did that for you, so give thanks to Allah for the blessings He has bestowed upon you in that respect, not to the gods and rivals, for you have made partners with Him in thanks, whereas He has no partner in the blessings He has bestowed upon you.

* *

As for His words ﴿And Allah brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers, knowing nothing﴾:

This is a complete sentence; then the statement is begun, and it is said: "And Allah made for you hearing, sight, and hearts." We say this is so because Allah, exalted is His remembrance, made worship, hearing, sight, and hearts before He brought them forth from their mothers' wombs, whereas He gave them knowledge and understanding only after He had brought them forth from their mothers' wombs.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 79:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Have they not seen the birds, made subservient in the air of the sky? None holds them up except Allah. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.﴾

Allah, the Exalted, says to these polytheists: Have you not seen, O polytheists who associate others with Allah, the birds made subservient in the air of the sky, meaning: in the atmosphere of the sky between it and the earth, as Ibrahim ibn Imran al-Ansari said:

"Woe to its mother, from the air of the atmosphere, seeking, / And not like that which in the earth is sought."

[[The verse is attributed by the author to Ibrahim ibn Imran al-Ansari. Al-Baghdadi, in al-Khizanah (2: 112), attributes it to Imru' al-Qays ibn Hujr al-Kindi. In the Kitab, Sibawayh attributes it once to Imru' al-Qays (1: 353) and once (2: 272) to al-Nu'man ibn Bashir al-Ansari. Al-Baghdadi mentioned the qit'ah (poem fragment) of which this verse is part, which consists of ten verses, and attributed it to Imru' al-Qays, and its opening is: "The good is whatever the sun rises and sets upon, / a seeking amid the sides of horses, bound."

The verse of evidence is the eighth in the fragment, and its beginning is: "Not like the one in the air..." etc. Ibn Rashiq said in al-'Umdah: this verse, according to Di'bil, is the most excellent verse the Arabs ever composed, and by it he preferred it over the poets. As for his saying "wailuhha" (woe to it): this is in the form of a curse upon a thing, but the intended meaning is wonder. The feminine pronoun refers to the eagle. Al-Jaw: what lies between the sky and the earth. By "the sought" he meant the wolf, because he described an eagle that pursued a wolf to hunt it, so he marvelled at its intense pursuit, and marvelled at the wolf too for its speed and its strong flight from it.

The author cited the verse when explaining His saying (Have they not seen the birds made subservient in the air of the sky), i.e., in the atmosphere of the sky between it and the earth, just as Abu 'Ubaydah before him cited it in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 365) to show that jaw al-sama' means the air.]]

Meaning: in the atmosphere of the sky. ﴿None holds them up except Allah﴾ means: their flight in the air is only by Allah, and by His subjecting them to that; were He to take from them the flight He gave them, they would not be able to rise up high.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe﴾

He says: Indeed in Allah's subjecting the birds, and enabling them to fly in the air of the sky, are clear signs and proofs that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that the idols and images have no share in divinity. ﴿For a people who believe﴾ means: for a people who acknowledge what their eyes witness and their senses perceive.

Concerning this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿subservient in the air of the sky﴾: i.e., in the midst (kabd) of the sky.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 80:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from your houses, a place of rest; and He has made for you, from the hides of livestock, tents that you find light [to carry] on the day you travel and the day you camp; and from their wool, their fur, and their hair [He has provided] furnishings and provision for a time.﴾

He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And Allah has made for you﴾ O people, ﴿from your houses﴾ which are of stone and clay, ﴿a place of rest﴾ in which you dwell during the days of your residence in your homes and lands. ﴿And He has made for you, from the hides of livestock, tents﴾ meaning the tents made of leather mats and of felt, hair, wool and fur. ﴿That you find light﴾ he says: you find it light to carry and to move, ﴿on the day you travel﴾ from your lands and cities for your journeys, ﴿and the day you camp﴾ in your lands and cities. ﴿And from their wool, their fur, and their hair [He has provided] furnishings﴾.

Commentators have said in the meaning of "rest" similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us. And al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿a place of rest from your houses﴾, he said: you rest in it.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

As for "al-ash'ar" (hair), it is the plural of "sha'r," whose ayn may be pronounced heavy or light, and the singular of "sha'r" is "sha'rah." As for "al-athath" (furnishings), it is the household goods of a house, and no singular of it has been heard; it is, in having no singular, like "al-mata'" (goods). It has been reported from some grammarians that he used to say: the singular of "athath" is "athathah," but I have not seen the people of knowledge of the Arabic language recognise this.

As evidence that "athath" means "mata'" (goods), there is the saying of the poet:

"The litters (of women) stirred you up, the day they departed, with the fine appearance of the furnishings."

[The verse belongs to Muhammad ibn Numayr al-Thaqafi, who used to write amorous verses about Zaynab, sister of al-Hajjaj ibn Yusuf al-Thaqafi, so he threatened him and he fled from him (his report is in al-Kamil of al-Mubarrad, p. 289), and the verse is from a poem of his (al-Kamil, p. 376). In (Lisan: ra'a) it says: al-Farra' said: al-Ri'y means the appearance, and the people of Medina recite the verse (wa-ri'an) without a hamza. He said: it is a good reading from ra'aytu, because it is from words whose final letters are not hamzated. Al-Jawhari said: whoever pronounces it with a hamza makes it from al-manzar (appearance) from ra'aytu, and it is what the eye sees of a good condition and an apparent dress. Abu Ubayd recited for Muhammad ibn Numayr al-Thaqafi: "The litters stirred you up the day they departed, with the fine appearance of the furnishings." As for whoever does not pronounce the hamza: either it is by lightening the hamza, or it is from "ruwiyat alwanuhum wa-julūduhum," i.e., they became full and beautiful. "Athathan" means "mata'an" (goods). Abu Ubayda said this in Majaz al-Qur'an (1: 365).]

It is also narrated with the variant "bidhi al-zayy." I see that the origin of "athath" is the gathering of some goods together until they become abundant, like "al-sha'r al-athith," which is abundant and dense; it is said of it: "aththha sha'ru fulan yath'ithu athan," when a man's hair becomes abundant, dense and gathered.

Commentators have said in the meaning of this similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying "athath": by "athath" he means wealth.

- Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us. And al-Harith related to me, he said: al-Hasan related to us, he said: Warqa related to us. And al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq informed us, he said: Abdullah related to us, from Warqa, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿athath﴾, he said: goods.

- Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿athath﴾, he said: it is wealth.

- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abdullah ibn Harb al-Razi related to us, he said: Salamah informed us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman, regarding His saying ﴿athath﴾, he said: clothing.

* *

As for His saying ﴿and provision for a time﴾:

It means that He made that for them as a provision, by which they subsist and are sufficed until the time of their death.

As:

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, ﴿and provision for a time﴾: it means adornment; he says: they benefit from it until a time.

- Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿and provision for a time﴾, he said: until death.

- Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, he said: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿and provision for a time﴾: until a term and a sustenance.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 81:

The discussion of the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He has created, shades, and He has made for you among the mountains shelters, and He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat, and garments that protect you from your violence. Thus does He complete His favor upon you, that you may submit (to Him).﴾

His saying, Exalted is His remembrance: Among the favors of Allah upon you, O people, is that He has made for you, from what He created of trees and other things, shades under which you seek shade from the intense heat. The word is the plural of ẓill (shade).

Interpreters of the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: ʿAmr narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿from what He created, shades﴾: He said: the trees.

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He created, shades﴾: Yes, by Allah, from the trees and from other things.

* *

And His saying ﴿and He has made for you among the mountains shelters﴾

He says: And He has made for you, among the mountains, places where you dwell, and it is the plural of kinn (shelter).

As follows:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, His saying (and He has made for you among the mountains shelters): He says: caves in the mountains in which one dwells.

﴿And He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat﴾ means garments of cotton, linen and wool, and their shirts.

As follows:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿And He has made for you garments that protect you from the heat﴾: of cotton, linen and wool.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾: He said: cotton and linen.

* *

And His saying ﴿and garments that protect you from your violence﴾

He says: and coats of mail that protect you from your violence. Violence (baʾs) means war, and the meaning is: they protect you, in your violence, from weapons reaching you.

As follows:

- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, ﴿and garments that protect you from your violence﴾: of this iron.

- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, ﴿and garments that protect you from your violence﴾: He said: they are garments of iron.

* *

And His saying ﴿Thus does He complete His favor upon you, that you may submit﴾

He, Exalted is His remembrance, says: Just as your Lord gave you these things which He described in these verses as a favor from Him to you, so He completes His favor upon you, that you may submit. That is: that you may humble yourselves before Allah in obedience, and that souls among you may be humbled in His monotheism, and that you may make worship sincerely for Him. It has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he used to recite ﴿la-ʿallakum taslamūn﴾ with a fatḥah on the tā'.

- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Handhalah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: ﴿la-ʿallakum taslamūn﴾, he said: meaning, from wounds.

- Ahmad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated to us, saying: ʿAbbad ibn al-ʿAwwam narrated to us, from Handhalah al-Sadusi, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that he recited it: ﴿la-ʿallakum taslamūn﴾, from wounds. Ahmad ibn Yusuf said: Abu ʿUbayd said: meaning with a fatḥah on the tā' and the lām.

So the interpretation of the statement according to this reading of Ibn ʿAbbas is: Thus does He complete His favor upon you by what He made for you of garments that protect you from your violence, so that you may be safe from weapons in your wars. But the reading that I do not permit to be departed from is with a ḍammah on the tā' in His saying ﴿la-ʿallakum tuslimūn﴾ and a kasrah on the lām, from aslama (to submit), because of the consensus of the authorities among the readers of the great cities upon it.

If someone says to us: How did He make garments for you that protect you from the heat, singling out the heat by mention rather than the cold, when they protect against both heat and cold? Or how was it said ﴿and He has made for you among the mountains shelters﴾ while leaving out what He made for them of the plains? It is said to him: The reason for which the revelation came in this manner has been disputed, and we will mention what has been said about that, then indicate which of the sayings is most correct.

It has been narrated from ʿAṭāʾ al-Khurasani concerning that:

- Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, from ʿUthman ibn ʿAtaʾ, from his father, who said: The Qur'an was only revealed according to the measure of their understanding. Do you not see the saying of Allah, Exalted is His remembrance: ﴿And Allah has made for you, from what He created, shades, and He has made for you among the mountains shelters﴾, while what He made for them of the plains is greater and more abundant? But they were people of mountains. Do you not see His saying ﴿and from their wool and their furs and their hair, furnishings and provision for a time﴾? And what He made for them other than that is greater and more abundant, but they were people of fur and hair. Do you not see His saying ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains of hail in them﴾, which amazes them with that? And what is sent down of snow is greater and more abundant, but they did not know it. Do you not see His saying ﴿garments that protect you from the heat﴾, while what protects from the cold is more and greater? But they were people of heat. So the reason why Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, singled out the garments as protecting from heat rather than cold, according to this saying, is that those addressed were people of heat. Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, mentioned His favor upon them by what protects them from the harm by which they knew harm, rather than what they did not know the extent of harm of. And so it is with the rest of the letters.

Others said: He mentioned that specifically, relying on the mention of one of them to indicate the other, since its meaning was known to those addressed, and that garments which protect from the heat also protect from the cold. They said: This exists and is used in the speech of the Arabs, and they cited for their view the verse of a poet:

*And I do not know, when I set my face toward a thing, seeking good, which of the two will beset me.*

[The verse is among the evidences of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an (p. 176), where he said: "His saying (garments that protect you from the heat), without saying 'and the cold', was left out because its meaning is known, and Allah knows best, like the saying of the poet: 'And I do not know ... the verse.' He means that good and evil beset me, because when he seeks good, he guards against evil." The poet made his meaning clear in the following verse, which agrees with what they said: *Is it the good that I seek, or the evil that seeks me?* Both verses are by Suhaym ibn Wathil al-Riyahi, from a poem beginning: *Fatima, before your parting, grant me enjoyment, and your refusal of what I asked, as if you were to make me your enemy.*]

So he said: "which of the two beset me", meaning good or evil, and he mentioned the good only because when one seeks good, one guards against evil.

The most correct of the two sayings concerning this is the saying of those who said that the people were addressed according to the measure of their understanding, even though mention of some of it indicates what was left unmentioned for one who knows both the mentioned and the omitted. That is because Allah, Exalted is His remembrance, only enumerated the favors which He bestowed upon those targeted by address in this surah rather than others, so He mentioned His bounties towards them.

The Interpretation of His Words, the Exalted: ﴿So if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance (of the message). They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it, and most of them are disbelievers.﴾ (82–83)

The Exalted says, speaking of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): If these polytheists turn their backs, O Muhammad, on what I have sent you with of truth to them, and do not respond to you and turn away from it, then there is no blame or reproach upon you, for you have discharged what is incumbent upon you in this matter; there is upon you only the conveyance to them of what you were sent with. By His words ﴿al-mubin﴾ (the clear), He means that which makes it clear to whoever hears it, so that he understands it.

As for His words ﴿They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the meaning of the favour which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned, that these polytheists deny despite their recognition of it. Some of them said: It is the Prophet (ﷺ). They recognized his prophethood, then they rejected it and called him a liar.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, he said: Muhammad (ﷺ).

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, the like of it.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is that they recognize that what Allah, the Exalted, enumerated in this surah of blessings is from Allah, and that Allah is the One who bestowed those upon them, but they deny that, claiming that they inherited it from their fathers.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, he said: It is the dwellings, the livestock, and what they are provided from them, and the garments of iron and clothing. The disbelievers of Quraysh recognize this, then they deny it by saying: This was for our fathers, and they bestowed it upon us (furrawhuna) [[Ibn Manzur said in al-Lisan: In the hadith of Umm Zar': "and he gave me abundant camels" — i.e., gave me. He said: al-tarwih is like al-ihrah (granting).]] it.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, similar to that, except that he said: and they inherited it for us (fa-warrathunaha). And in the report from Ibn Jurayj he added: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: They know that Allah created them and gave them what He gave them; so their recognition of His favour and then their denial of it is their disbelief thereafter.

Others said regarding this:

Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu Ishaq al-Fazari, from Layth, from 'Awn ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah, regarding ﴿They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, he said: Their denial of it is that a man says: Had it not been for so-and-so, such-and-such would not have happened, and had it not been for so-and-so, I would not have obtained such-and-such.

Others said: The meaning of that is that when the disbelievers are asked: Who provides for you? they acknowledge that Allah is the One who provided for them, then they deny that by saying: Our provision came through the intercession of our gods.

The most correct of these views regarding the truth, and the most fitting to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of the one who said: By the favour mentioned by Allah in His words ﴿They recognize the favour of Allah﴾ is meant the favour upon them through the sending of Muhammad (ﷺ) to them, calling them to what he was sent with, and that this verse lies between two verses both of which are information about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and what he was sent with. So the most appropriate thing is that what lies between them should be in the sense of what precedes it and what follows it, since there is no indication that it departs from what precedes or follows it. What precedes this verse is His words ﴿So if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance. They recognize the favour of Allah, then they deny it﴾, and what follows it is ﴿And on the Day We raise up from every nation a witness﴾, and he is its Messenger. If that is so, then the meaning of the verse is: These polytheists, who acknowledge Allah, recognize the favour of Allah upon them through you, O Muhammad, then they deny you and reject your prophethood. ﴿And most of them are the disbelievers﴾ means: and most of your people are those who reject your prophethood, not those who affirm it.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "And [mention] the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness. Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved, nor will they be asked to make amends." (16:84)

He, the Exalted, says: They recognize the blessing of God, then deny it today and disown it. "On the Day We raise up from every nation a witness," and he is the one who bears witness against them that they answered the summons of God, namely their Messenger who was sent to them. "Then permission will not be given to those who disbelieved," meaning: then those who disbelieved will not be permitted to offer excuses, so that they might make excuses for having disbelieved in God and His Messenger. "Nor will they be asked to make amends," meaning they will not be given the chance to return to the world, so that they might repent and turn back in penitence. This is like His words, the Exalted: "This is a Day when they will not speak, nor will they be given permission so that they may make excuses." (77:35–36)

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said what is similar to what we have said about this.

Those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "And [mention] the Day We will raise up from every nation a witness," that the witness is their prophet, testifying that he had conveyed the messages of his Lord. God, the Exalted, said: "And We bring you as a witness against these." (4:41)

* *

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: "And when those who did wrong see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved." (16:85)

He, the Exalted, says: And when those who denied you, O Muhammad, and rejected your prophethood, and the nations who followed the way of the polytheists of your people, witness the punishment of God, nothing will save them from the punishment of God, because they will not be given permission to offer excuses, so that the punishment might be lightened for them by the excuse they claim. "Nor will they be reprieved" means: nor will they be delayed in punishment, because the time for repentance and turning back has passed; that is not the time for them, but rather the time for recompense for deeds. So they will not be granted respite in order to be reproached and then repent.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 86–87:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿When those who associated partners with God see their partners, they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners whom we used to invoke besides You." But they will throw back at them the word, "Indeed, you are liars."﴾ (86)

His saying, exalted is He, means: When the polytheists see on the Day of Resurrection what they used to worship besides God, of deities, idols and other things, they will say, "Our Lord, these are our partners in disbelief in You, and the partners we used to invoke as gods besides You." God, exalted is He, said: ﴿they threw back﴾, meaning: their partners whom they used to worship besides God, ﴿the word﴾, meaning: they said to them, "Indeed, you are liars, O polytheists, we never called you to worship us."

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us; and al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿they threw back to them the word﴾, he said: "They spoke to them."

His saying, exalted is He, means: The polytheists will offer submission to God on that Day, meaning: they will submit that day and be humbled before His judgment concerning them. Their deities that they used to invoke besides God in the world will not avail them, and they will disown them, nor will their people or their clans who used to defend them in the world. The Arabs say: "I threw to him such-and-such," meaning by it: "I said to him."

* *

As for His saying, ﴿and that which they used to fabricate vanished from them﴾:

It means: what they used to hope for from their deities, of intercession with God for salvation, failed them.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.
