Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said so:

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying, ﴿And they will offer submission to God that Day﴾, he said: "They will be humbled and submit that day," ﴿and that which they used to fabricate vanished from them﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 88:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the way of Allah — We will increase them in punishment upon punishment for what they used to spread corruption.﴾

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Those who denied, O Muhammad, your prophethood and called you a liar concerning what you brought them from your Lord, and who averted [others] from faith in Allah and His Messenger, and whoever desired [that], We will increase them in punishment on the Day of Resurrection in Hell, upon the punishment they are already in, before it was increased for them. It has also been said: that increase which Allah promised to add for them is scorpions and serpents.

Mention of those who said that:

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, he said: Scorpions with fangs like palm trees.

* Ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

* Ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah and Ibn ʿUyaynah narrated to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, regarding ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, he said: They will be increased with scorpions having fangs like tall palm trees.

* Ibrahim ibn Yaʿqub al-Jawzajani narrated to us, saying: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash informed us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

* Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Sulayman, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Murrah, from Masruq, from ʿAbd Allah, similarly.

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Israʾil narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said regarding ﴿We will increase them in punishment upon punishment﴾, he said: Vipers.

* Ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, from Israʾil, from al-Suddi, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: Vipers in the Fire.

* Ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Murrah, from ʿAbd Allah, the like of it.

* Mujahid ibn Musa and al-Fadl ibn al-Sabbah narrated to us, both saying: Jaʿfar ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: al-Aʿmash informed us, from Mujahid, from ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr, who said: Indeed, Hell has pits in which are serpents like Bukht camels [[al-Bukht: the Khurasani camels, which are camels with long necks; its singular is bukhti (Lisan al-ʿArab).]] and scorpions like dark-coloured mules. The people of the Fire will cry out for help to those pits or the shore, and they will leap upon them and seize their lips and their jaws down to their feet, so they will flee from them into the Fire, saying: "The Fire! The Fire!" Then they will be pursued until they feel its heat, and they will return. He said: They are in swarms.

* Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Huyayy ibn ʿAbd Allah informed me, from Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr, who said: Indeed, Hell has shores in which are serpents and scorpions whose necks are like the necks of Bukht camels.

* * *

As for His words ﴿for what they used to spread corruption﴾:

He says: We increase them with that punishment upon what they already suffer, for what they used to spread corruption, that is, for what they disobeyed Allah in the world and commanded His servants to disobey Him; that was their corruption. O Allah, we ask You for well-being, O Master of this world and the everlasting Hereafter.

The Interpretation of His words, the Exalted: {And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves, and We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.} [16:89]

He, the Exalted, says: {And on the Day We raise up in every nation a witness against them from among themselves}, meaning: We will question their prophet whom We sent to them to call them to obedience to Us. He said {from among themselves} because He, the Exalted, used to send to the nations prophets from among them. [We will ask them]: What did they answer you, and what did they reply to you? {And We bring you, [O Muhammad], as a witness against these}, meaning He says to His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ: And We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness against your people and your nation to whom We sent you, regarding what they answered you with, and what they did concerning what We sent you with to them.

* *

And His words {And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things}:

He says: This Qur'an was sent down to you, O Muhammad, as a clarification of everything people need to know of what is lawful and unlawful, of reward and punishment, {and as guidance} from misguidance, {and mercy} for whoever believes in it and acts upon what it contains of the limits of Allah, His commands and His prohibitions, so that he makes lawful what He made lawful and forbids what He forbade, {and good tidings for the Muslims}, meaning: a glad tiding for whoever obeys Allah and submits to Him in monotheism and yields to Him in obedience, giving him good news of His abundant reward in the Hereafter and His great honor.

And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said:

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, he said: Aban ibn Taghlib related to us, from al-Hakam, from Mujahid, {clarification for all things}: He said: "[It is clarification of] what He made lawful and unlawful."

⁕ Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, from Ibn 'Uyayna, from Aban ibn Taghlib, from Mujahid, regarding His words {clarification for all things}: "[Of] what He made lawful for them and forbade for them."

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, he said: Abu Ahmad related to us, he said: Sufyan related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, His words {clarification for all things}, he said: "[Of] what He commanded and what He forbade."

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words {And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things}, he said: "[Of] what they were commanded and what they were forbidden."

⁕ Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ash'ath, from a man, who said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Every knowledge and everything has been explained to us in this Qur'an." Then he recited this verse.

The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives, and forbids immorality and bad conduct and oppression. He admonishes you that you may remember.﴾

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Indeed, Allah commands in this Book which He has sent down to you, O Muhammad, justice, which is equity. Among equity is acknowledging the One who has bestowed His blessing upon us, thanking Him for His bounty, and ascribing praise to its rightful owner. If that is justice, and the idols and images have no favour with us that deserves praise, then it would be ignorance on our part to praise them and worship them, for they neither bestow blessings so as to be thanked, nor benefit so as to be worshipped. Thus it is incumbent upon us to bear witness that there is no god but Allah, alone, without partner. For this reason, those who said so stated that justice in this context is the testimony that there is no god but Allah.

Mention of those who said that: Al-Muthanna and ʿAli ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct﴾, he said: "The testimony that there is no god but Allah." And His words "and good conduct": the good conduct which the Exalted commanded alongside the justice we have described is patience toward Allah in obedience to what He has commanded and forbidden, in hardship and ease, in what is disliked and what is liked, and that is the performance of His obligations.

As follows:

Al-Muthanna and ʿAli ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿and good conduct﴾, he said: "The performance of the obligations."

* *

And His words ﴿and giving to relatives﴾

He says: and giving the relatives the right which Allah has obligated upon you because of kinship and ties of blood.

As follows:

Al-Muthanna and ʿAli related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿and giving to relatives﴾, he said: "The wombs (kinship ties)."

* *

And His words ﴿and forbids immorality﴾

He said: Immorality (al-fahshaʾ) in this place means fornication (al-zina).

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Muthanna and ʿAli ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿and forbids immorality﴾, he said: "Fornication." We have already explained the meaning of al-fahshaʾ with its evidence earlier.

* *

And His words ﴿and oppression﴾

It was said: By al-baghy (oppression) in this place is meant arrogance and wrongdoing.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Muthanna and ʿAli ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿and oppression﴾, he said: "Arrogance and wrongdoing." The root of al-baghy is transgression and exceeding the measure and limit of anything. We have already explained this earlier.

* *

And His words ﴿He admonishes you that you may remember﴾

He says: Your Lord reminds you, O people, so that you may remember and turn back to His command and prohibition, and recognize the truth for its people.

As follows:

Al-Muthanna and ʿAli ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: ʿAbd Allah related to us, saying: Muʿawiya related to me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding ﴿He admonishes you﴾, he said: "He instructs you." ﴿That you may remember﴾.

It has been reported from Ibn ʿUyayna that he used to say in interpreting this: the meaning of justice in this place is the equality of inner intention and outward conduct in every doer who acts for Allah; the meaning of good conduct is that one's inner intention is better than one's outward conduct; and that immorality and wrongdoing are when one's outward conduct is better than one's inner intention.

It has been reported from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud that he used to say regarding this verse:

Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard Mansur ibn al-Nuʿman, from ʿAmir, from Shatir ibn Shakal, saying: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: "Indeed, the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an is in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives﴾ ... to the end of the verse."

Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from al-Shaʿbi, from Sutayr ibn Shakal, saying: I heard ʿAbd Allah say: "Indeed, the most comprehensive verse in the Qur'an for good or for evil is the verse in Surah al-Nahl: ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct﴾ ... the verse."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Indeed, Allah orders justice and good conduct and giving to relatives﴾ ... the verse: "There is no good character that the people of the Jahiliyya used to practise and esteem except that Allah commanded it, and there is no bad character that they used to reproach one another for except that Allah forbade it and warned against it. He only forbade the base and blameworthy characters."

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 91:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a pledge, and do not break oaths after their confirmation, and you have already made God your surety over you. Indeed, God knows what you do.﴾ (16:91)

His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: Fulfil the compact of God when you enter into a compact with Him, and His pact when you make a pact with Him, so that you thereby make it binding upon yourselves to fulfil a right owed to the one with whom you made the pact and with whom you pledged. ﴿And do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ means: do not violate the matter over which you have sworn oaths in mutual agreement, meaning after you have strengthened the oaths upon yourselves, so that you break your oaths, lie in them, and annul them after confirming them. From this one says: "Walid (fulan) confirmed his oath, yuwakkiduha, tawkeedan," meaning he strengthened it. This is the dialect of the people of the Hijaz; as for the people of Najd, they say: "akkadtuha, u'akkiduha, ta'keedan."

* *

His saying: ﴿And you have already made God your surety over you﴾

He means: you have made God, by fulfilling what you have contracted upon yourselves, a guardian who watches over the one among you who fulfils the covenant of God which He pledged to uphold, and over the one who breaks it.

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said, although they differ concerning who is meant by this verse and what it was revealed about. Some of them said: it refers to those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God ﷺ upon Islam, and it was revealed concerning them.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Ammara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Musa told us, saying: Abu Layla informed us, from Buraydah, regarding His words ﴿And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a pledge﴾, he said: This verse was revealed concerning the pledge of the Prophet ﷺ. Whoever embraced Islam pledged allegiance upon Islam. They said: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of God when you have made a pledge﴾ is this pledge which you pledged upon Islam, ﴿and do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾ the pledge, so let not the scarcity of Muhammad ﷺ and his companions and the abundance of the polytheists lead you to break the pledge which you made upon Islam, even if they were few and the polytheists were many.

Others said: it was revealed concerning the alliance which the people of polytheism had concluded in the Jahiliyya, and God, mighty and majestic, commanded them in Islam to fulfil it and not to break it.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of God, exalted is He, ﴿and do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾, he said: their stringent application in oaths.

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq told us, saying: 'Abdullah told us, from Warqa', all together, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾, he says: after their strengthening and stringent application.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: These were people who were allies of a people with whom they had made an alliance, and some of them gave a covenant. Then other people came to them and said: We are more numerous, mightier and more powerful, so break the covenant of these people and return to us, and they did so. That is the saying of God, exalted is He: ﴿and do not break oaths after their confirmation, and you have already made God your surety over you﴾ — [that] one community should be more numerous than another community; [and when] one community is more numerous, you break the covenant between yourselves and these people, so this is the case of that.

Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam told us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: I asked Yahya ibn Sa'id regarding the saying of God, ﴿and do not break oaths after their confirmation﴾, and he said: the covenants.

The correct view on this matter is to say: God, exalted is He, in this verse commanded His servants to fulfil the covenants which they make upon themselves, and forbade them from breaking oaths after confirming them upon themselves for others, by agreements made among them in truth, of what God does not dislike. It is permissible that it was revealed concerning those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God ﷺ, forbidding them to break their pledge out of fear of the fewness of the Muslims' numbers and the abundance of the polytheists' numbers; and that it was revealed concerning those who wanted to shift their alliance away from their allies for the sake of fewness of their numbers relative to others who were more numerous; and it is permissible that it concerns something other than that. There is no report by which proof is established that it was revealed concerning one of these rather than another; nor is there any indication in the Book or any rational proof as to which of these was meant by it, and no view on this is more deserving of truth than what we have said, because its apparent meaning indicates it, and because the verse was revealed for some cause, and its ruling is general over everything that carries the meaning of the cause for which it was revealed.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿and you have already made God your surety over you﴾, he said: a guardian (wakil).

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, God knows what you do﴾

He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Indeed God, O people, knows what you do regarding the covenants which you make with God, of fulfilling them, and the alliances and oaths which you confirm upon yourselves, whether you are faithful in them or break them, and other of your actions. He takes account of all of it upon you; He will question you about it and about what you did concerning it. He means: beware of God lest you meet Him having opposed His command and prohibition in them, and thereby deserve from Him what you have no power to bear of His painful punishment.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 92:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿And be not like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong, into separate strands, taking your oaths as a means of deception between you, so that one community may be more numerous than another community. Allah only tests you thereby. And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ.﴾

Exalted is He, says: forbidding His servants from breaking oaths after confirming them, and commanding them to fulfil covenants, and presenting as a parable for the one who breaks that a woman who unravels her thread after its twisting and undoes it after its firm making: "And do not be, O people, in breaking your oaths after their confirmation and after you have given Allah your pledge to fulfil that, like the covenants and pacts. ﴿Like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong﴾, meaning: after its firm twisting." Some of the scholars of Arabic said: "al-Quwwah (strength) is that which is spun in a single strand and not doubled." It was said that the one who used to do this was a well-known foolish woman in Makkah.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me: ﴿like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong﴾ He said: "She was a foolish woman in Makkah who would unravel it after she had twisted it."

Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Sadaqah, from al-Suddi: ﴿And be not like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong, into separate strands, taking your oaths as a means of deception between you﴾ He said: "She was a foolish woman in Makkah who, whenever she twisted her thread, would unravel it."

Others said: this is only a parable which Allah struck for the one who breaks a covenant, likening him to a woman who does this act. And regarding the meaning of "unravels her thread after it has been made strong," they said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿And be not like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong, into separate strands﴾ "If you heard of a woman who unravelled her thread after twisting it, you would say: How foolish this woman is! And this is a parable which Allah struck for the one who breaks his covenant."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong﴾ He said: "Her thread: her rope, which she unravels after twisting it and from which she derives no benefit afterwards."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong﴾ He said: "She unravelled her rope after firm twisting and strength."

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿And be not like her who unravels her thread after it has been made strong, into separate strands﴾ "This is a parable which Allah struck for the one who breaks the covenant he gives. Allah struck this parable for him with the likeness of the woman who spun then unravelled her thread. He gave them a pledge and then went back, so he broke the covenant he had given them."

* *

As for His words ﴿into separate strands (ankathan)﴾

Meaning: unravelled pieces. Everything that is undone after being twisted is ankath, and its singular is nakth, whether it is a rope or a thread. One says from it: "Fulan unravelled this rope (nakatha), so he unravels it (yankuthuhu) unravelling (nakthan)," and a rope is "muntakith" when its strength has come undone. In this place, what is meant by it is the breaking of a pledge and a bond.

* *

As for His words ﴿taking your oaths as a means of deception between you, so that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾

Exalted is He, says: you make your oaths, by which you swear that you will fulfil the covenant to those with whom you have made it, ﴿a means of deception between you﴾, meaning: trickery and delusion, so that they may feel secure in you while you conceal treachery for them and abandonment of the fulfilment of the covenant, and a shift from them to others because the others are more numerous than they are. And "dakhal" in the speech of the Arabs is every matter that is not sound. One says from it: "I know the dakhal (inner corruption) of so-and-so, and his duklul, and his dakhilah (hidden matter), and his dakhalah and dakhilah."

As for His words ﴿so that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾, "arba" is the comparative form of "riba" (increase). One says: "This is more (arba) than that and arba-'anhu," when it is more than it. And from it is the saying of the poet:

"And a dark, Khatti spear whose joints are like the stones of dry dates, which has exceeded ten spans in length..."

[Note: the verse is cited in Lisan al-Arab (qasab). It is said to be by Hatim al-Ta'i, though not found in his poetry. Arbi and Armi are two dialectal forms. Nawa al-qasab is the hardest of stones. Khatt is a place near Bahrain famous for spear-making. The author cites the verse to show that arba means "more." Abu Ubaydah likewise said so in Majaz al-Quran.]

One says only "arba fulan min hadha wa dhalika" because of the increase he adds over his creditor beyond the principal.

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Muthanna and Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, both saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾ He said: "more numerous."

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾ He said: "people more numerous than people."

Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾ He said: "They used to make alliances with allies, then find others more numerous and mightier than them, so they would break the alliance of these and make alliance with those who were mightier than them. So they were forbidden from this."

Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid [meaning: the like of it; he often gives the chain and omits the text when it has already been mentioned, and does not give a phrase like "the like of it" or "similar"; reference to some of this was made earlier in its places], and al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words ﴿taking your oaths as a means of deception between you﴾ He said: "treachery and betrayal among you" ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾: that a people may be mightier and more numerous than a people.

Ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Abu Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿dakhalan baynakum﴾ He said: "treachery among you."

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿taking your oaths as a means of deception between you﴾: "He deceives with them; he gives him the pledge, assures him, and brings him down from his safe place, so his foot slips while he is secure. Then he returns intending betrayal." He said: "The first beginning of this was a people who were allies of a people. They made alliance and gave each other covenants. Then came people who said: 'We are more numerous, mightier, and more protected,' so they broke the covenant of these and returned to us, and they did so. This is the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And do not break the oaths after their confirmation, and you have made Allah your surety over you﴾ ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾ 'arba: more, because these were more numerous than those, you broke the covenant between you and these, so this was in this. And the other matter concerns the one who makes a covenant with someone, then brings him down from his fortress and then breaks it upon him. The first verse concerns these people, and it is their beginning, and the other concerns this."

It was narrated from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, regarding His words ﴿that one community may be more numerous than another community﴾: "more," meaning: so you must fulfil the covenant.

* *

As for His words ﴿Allah only tests you thereby﴾

Exalted is He, says: Allah only tests you by His command to you to fulfil the covenant of Allah when you make a pact, so that the obedient among you who submits to His command and prohibition may be distinguished from the disobedient who opposes His command and prohibition. ﴿And He will surely make clear to you on the Day of Resurrection that over which you used to differ﴾. Exalted is He, says: And He will surely make clear to you, O people, your Lord, on the Day of Resurrection when you come before Him, by recompensing each group of you for its deeds in the world, the good-doer among you for his goodness and the evildoer for his evil. ﴿That over which you used to differ﴾: what they used to differ about in the world was that the believer in Allah affirmed the oneness of Allah and the prophethood of His Prophet, and believed in what His prophets were sent with, while the disbeliever denied all of that. That was their difference in the world, which Allah, the Exalted, promised His servants He would make clear to them when they come before Him, with the clarification we have described.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 93:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And had Allah willed, He would have made you one community, but He leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: Had your Lord, O people, willed to show you kindness by granting you success from Him, you would all have been one group and one people of one religion, not differing and not dividing. But He, the Exalted, made you differ, and made you people of various religions: He granted success to these people to believe in Him and to act in obedience to Him, so they became believers, and He forsook those people and withheld His success from them, so they became disbelievers. And Allah will surely question all of you on the Day of Resurrection about what you used to do in the world, regarding what He commanded you and forbade you. Then He will recompense you: the obedient among you with the reward of their obedience, and the disobedient to Him with the consequence of their disobedience.

The exegesis of the verse: "And do not make your oaths a means of deceit among yourselves, lest a foot slip after being firmly planted and you taste evil for having barred [others] from the way of God, and there will be a great punishment for you" (16:94).

God, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "And do not make your oaths a means of deceit (dakhal) and treachery among yourselves, by which you deceive people," ﴿so that a foot slips after being firmly planted﴾, meaning: "so that you perish after having been safe from destruction." This is an image (mathal) for every person afflicted after well-being, or who falls into peril after safety, and similar cases: "his foot slipped," as the poet said:

*"The lead will prevent you from winning, if you are a leader,
and you will be struck on the rear if your sandals slip beneath you."*

[Note: In (Lisan al-Arab, root l-ṭ-ʿ): al-laṭʿ is to strike a person's rear with your foot. You say: "I struck him (with a kasra) and I strike him with a laṭʿ." As for God's words, ﴿so that a foot slips after being firmly planted﴾, Abu Ubayda said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:367): it is a proverb said of everyone afflicted after well-being, or who falls into peril after safety, and the like: "his foot slipped."]

* *

As for His words, ﴿and you taste evil﴾:

He says: "and you yourselves taste evil." That evil is the punishment of God with which He punishes the people of His disobedience in this world, and that is part of what He punished the people of disbelief with. ﴿For having barred [others] from the way of God﴾, meaning: for having turned away from belief in God and His Messenger those who wished to believe. ﴿And there is a great punishment for you﴾ in the Hereafter, which is the Fire of Hell.

This verse indicates that the interpretation of Buraydah, which we mentioned from him regarding God's words ﴿And fulfill the covenant of God when you have made it﴾ and the verses that follow, is correct: that it refers to those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to Islam, [Note: "ʿan" here is causal, meaning "because of" the abandonment of Islam, like His words: "We will not abandon our gods for your sake" (11:53), i.e., for you.] who abandoned Islam because its adherents were few and the people of polytheism were many. The view that Mujahid stated, that they were meant by it, is not correct, because the shifting of a people who had made alliances from their allies to others besides them does not involve barring from the way of God or going astray from guidance. God, may His remembrance be exalted, has described in this verse the doers of that, that by making their oaths a means of deceit among themselves and breaking their oaths after confirming them, they are barriers against the way of God, and in the previous verse He described them as people of misguidance. This is the description of the people of disbelief in God, not the description of those who changed their alliance from one people to another.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 95–96:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew. What is with you will end, and what is with Allah will remain. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Do not break your covenants, O people, and your agreements that you have concluded with those with whom you have contracted, confirming them with your oaths, seeking by your breaking of them some worldly gain that is little. Rather, fulfil the covenant of Allah, which He has commanded you to fulfil; Allah will reward you for fulfilling it. Indeed, what is with Allah of reward for you for fulfilling that is better for you, if you only knew. It is the excess between the two exchanges: one of them is the small price, which you buy by breaking the covenant of Allah in this world, and the other is the abundant reward in the Hereafter for fulfilling it. Then He, the Exalted, explained the difference between the two exchanges and the excess between the two rewards, saying: What is with you, O people, of what you possess in this world, however much it is, is perishable and passing away; and what is with Allah for the one who fulfils His covenant and obeys Him of good things is enduring and not passing away. So for what is with Him, act, and for the remaining that does not perish, strive.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Allah will surely reward those who were patient in their obedience to Him, in ease and in hardship, with their reward on the Day of Resurrection for their patience in them and their hastening toward His pleasure, according to the best of what they used to do of deeds, not the worst of them; and Allah will surely forgive them their bad deeds by His grace.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 95–96:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew. What is with you will end, and what is with Allah will remain. And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Do not break your covenants, O people, and your agreements that you have concluded with those with whom you have contracted, confirming them with your oaths, seeking by your breaking of them some worldly gain that is little. Rather, fulfil the covenant of Allah, which He has commanded you to fulfil; Allah will reward you for fulfilling it. Indeed, what is with Allah of reward for you for fulfilling that is better for you, if you only knew. It is the excess between the two exchanges: one of them is the small price, which you buy by breaking the covenant of Allah in this world, and the other is the abundant reward in the Hereafter for fulfilling it. Then He, the Exalted, explained the difference between the two exchanges and the excess between the two rewards, saying: What is with you, O people, of what you possess in this world, however much it is, is perishable and passing away; and what is with Allah for the one who fulfils His covenant and obeys Him of good things is enduring and not passing away. So for what is with Him, act, and for the remaining that does not perish, strive.

* *

And His saying: ﴿And We will surely give those who were patient their reward according to the best of what they used to do.﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Allah will surely reward those who were patient in their obedience to Him, in ease and in hardship, with their reward on the Day of Resurrection for their patience in them and their hastening toward His pleasure, according to the best of what they used to do of deeds, not the worst of them; and Allah will surely forgive them their bad deeds by His grace.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 97:

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do.﴾ (16:97)

His words, exalted is His remembrance: Whoever acts in obedience to God and fulfils the covenants of God when he makes one, whether male or female, of the children of Adam, while he is a believer – that is, while he affirms the reward of God, which He promised to the people of His obedience for obedience, and the punishment of the people of disobedience for disobedience – ﴿then We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾.

The people of interpretation differed concerning what God meant by the good life which He promised these people He would give them. Some of them said: He means that He will give them life in this world, for as long as they live in it, with lawful provision.

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay' [Isma'il ibn Sumay', with a fatha on the sin, al-Hanafi, Abu Muhammad; a number of scholars declared him trustworthy, and he was a Kharijite], from Abu Malik and Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Good provision in this world.

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Good provision in this world.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, meaning in this world.

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Ibn 'Uyayna related to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Dahhak: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Good provision, lawful.

- 'Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil related to me, saying: 'Awn ibn Salam al-Qurashi related to us, saying: Bishr ibn 'Umara informed us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, regarding His words ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: He eats what is lawful and wears what is lawful.

Others said: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ means that We grant him contentment (qana'a).

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman related to us, from al-Minhal ibn Khalifa, from Abu Khuzayma Sulayman al-Tammar, from one he mentioned, from 'Ali: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Contentment.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Abu 'Isam related to us, from Abu Sa'id, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: The good life is contentment.

Others said: Rather, by the good life He means life as a believer in God, acting in His obedience.

Mention of those who said this:

- It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words (﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾): He who does a righteous deed while a believer, whether in want or in ease, his life is good; but he who turns away from the remembrance of God, does not believe, and does not do righteousness, his livelihood is straitened, with no good in it.

Others said: The good life is happiness.

Mention of those who said this:

- al-Muthanna and 'Ali ibn Dawud related to me, both saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, His words ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Happiness.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: life in Paradise.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Hawdha related to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: No life is good for anyone apart from Paradise.

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Abu Usama related to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: Life is not good for anyone except in Paradise.

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾: God does not accept a deed except with sincerity, and it requires that the deed be done in faith. God, exalted, said ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, and that is Paradise.

- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾, he said: The Hereafter; He gives them a good life in the Hereafter.

- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾: The good life in the Hereafter is Paradise, that is the good life. He said: ﴿And We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do﴾. And he said: Do you not see that He says ﴿Would that I had sent forth [good] for my life﴾? He said: This is its Hereafter. He also recited ﴿And indeed, the Hereafter – that is the [true] life﴾, and said: The Hereafter is an abode of life for the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise; there is no death in it for either group.

- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', regarding His words ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer﴾, he said: Faith is sincerity to God alone, and He made clear that He does not accept a deed except with sincerity toward Him.

The most correct of these interpretations is the view of those who say: its interpretation is: ﴿We will surely cause him to live a good life﴾ through contentment, because whoever is content by God with what He has apportioned to him of provision, his toil for this world does not increase, his fatigue in it does not grow great, and his life is not embittered in it by pursuing what he has missed of it and by his greed for what he may never attain in it.

I have said that this is the most apt interpretation of the verse because God, exalted is His remembrance, had threatened a people before it for their disobedience to Him: if they disobeyed Him, He would make them taste evil in this world and punishment in the Hereafter. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And do not take your oaths as means of deception among yourselves, lest a foot slip after being firmly planted and you taste evil for having averted [others] from the way of God﴾. This is for them in this world, and for them in the Hereafter there is a great punishment; this is for them in the Hereafter. Then He followed this with what applies to whoever fulfils the covenant of God and obeys Him, saying, exalted is He: what is with you ends, and what is with God remains. So the One who threatened the people of disobedience with tasting this evil, by His wisdom, willed that this promise to the people of His obedience be followed by goodness in this world and forgiveness in the Hereafter; and so God, exalted is His remembrance, did.

As for the report narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it means lawful provision, it is possible that its meaning is what we have said: that He contents him in this world with what He provides him from the lawful, even if it is little, so that his soul does not crave much of it from unlawful sources. It does not mean that He gives him abundant lawful provision, for we have seen that most of those who act for God in what pleases Him do not in this world receive abundant lawful provision, and we have found constriction of livelihood upon them to be more prevalent than abundance.

* *

As for His words ﴿and We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do﴾:

There is no doubt that this refers to the Hereafter, and so the people of interpretation said.

Mention of those who said this:

- Abu al-Sa'ib related to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do﴾, he said: When they arrive at God, He will reward them with their reward for the best of what they used to do.

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu Malik and Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and We will surely recompense them with their reward﴾, he said: In the Hereafter.

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Isma'il ibn Sumay', from Abu al-Rabi', from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿and We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do﴾, he says: He will recompense them with their reward in the Hereafter for the best of what they used to do.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning a people of various religious communities who boasted, each group saying: "We are better." God then made clear to them who the best of the communities are.

Mention of those who said this:

- Ibn Wakf' related to us, saying: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Salih, who said: People of idols, people of the Torah, and people of the Gospel sat together; these said: "We are better," and those said: "We are better." So God, exalted, revealed ﴿Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer – We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely recompense them with their reward for the best of what they used to do﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed (98). Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord (99). His authority is only over those who make him an ally and those who associate others with Him (100).﴾

Allah, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "When you, O Muhammad, are reciting the Qur'an, then seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyya) claimed that this is from what is delayed (al-mu'akhkhar) while its meaning is advanced (al-taqdim), and the meaning of the speech according to him is: "When you seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, then recite the Qur'an." But there is no basis for what he said, because if that were the case, whenever a seeker of refuge sought refuge from the accursed Satan, it would necessarily follow that he must recite the Qur'an. Rather, its meaning is what we have described, and His saying ﴿so seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾ is not a binding command; it is rather information and recommendation (nadb). This is because there is no disagreement among all that whoever recites the Qur'an without seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, whether before his recitation or after it, has not neglected an obligatory duty. Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we have said.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾: "This is an indication from Allah, the Exalted, which He has directed His servants to."

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, it means: Satan has no proof (hujja) against those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and act upon what Allah has commanded and refrain from what Allah has forbidden them. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾ means: they rely upon their Lord in the matters that befall them of their important affairs. ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾ means: his proof is only against those who worship him. ﴿And those who associate others with Him﴾ means: and those who associate others with Allah.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿His authority is only﴾ he said: "his proof."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾, he said: "They obey him."

The people of interpretation differed regarding the reason for which Satan was not given authority over the believer.

Some of them said, as was related to me from Waqid ibn Sulayman, from Sufyan, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, he said: "He has no authority to make them commit a sin that will not be forgiven."

Others said: it is the seeking of refuge; for when one seeks refuge in Allah, he is prevented from him and is not given authority over him, and they cited as evidence for the soundness of this view the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan comes to you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing﴾. The narration concerning that has already been mentioned in Surat al-Hijr.

Others said regarding this, with what:

al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾ up to His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: It is said that the enemy of Allah, Iblis, said ﴿I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾. So those are the ones over whom Satan has no way, and his authority is only over a people who took him as an ally and associated him in their deeds.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, he said: "The authority is over those who take Satan as a guardian and act in disobedience to Allah."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾, he said: "Those who obey him and worship him."

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and so seek refuge in Allah from him, by what Allah, the Exalted, has recommended of seeking refuge, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾ regarding whatever thoughts and whisperings come to them.

We have said this is the most correct interpretation of the verse because Allah, the Exalted, followed this statement with ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan comes to you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing﴾. Thus it became clear that He only recommended His servants to seek refuge from Him in these circumstances in order to protect them from his authority.

As for His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, the people of interpretation differed regarding its explanation. Some of them said, in agreement with what we said, that its meaning is: and those who associate others with Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, he said: "They equate others with the Lord of the worlds."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, he said: "They equate others with Allah."

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: "They made Iblis equal to their Lord, for they are associators with Allah."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "and those who associate others with Him" means they associated Satan in their deeds.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: "They associated him in their deeds."

The first view, namely the view of Mujahid, is the more correct of the two views regarding this, because those who take Satan as an ally only associate him with Allah in their worship, their sacrifices, their food and their drink, not that they associate Satan [with Allah as a partner]. Had the meaning of the speech been what al-Rabi' said, the wording would have been: "Those who are associators of him," and it would not have been "bihi" (with Him/with it)... so it would have been: "those who are associators of him in their deeds." Unless someone interprets the meaning of the speech to mean that the people used to hold the divinity of Satan and associate Allah with him in their worship of him, in which case the meaning of the speech would be sound, but it would depart from what the revelation brought in the rest of the Qur'an. For Allah, the Exalted, described the polytheists in the rest of the surahs of the Qur'an as having associated with Allah what He had not sent down any authority for, and in every place where He preceded to restrain them from that, He said: "Do not associate anything with Allah." We have not found in any part of the revelation: "Do not associate Allah with anything," nor in any part of the Qur'an, a report from Allah about them that they associated Allah with something. Therefore, it is permissible for us to direct the meaning of His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾ to mean "and those who associate Satan with Allah." Thus it is clear, since this is the case, that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾ refers to the Lord in His saying ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the accursed (98). Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord (99). His authority is only over those who make him an ally and those who associate others with Him (100).﴾

Allah, dhikruhu, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "When you, O Muhammad, are reciting the Qur'an, then seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan." Some of the grammarians (ahl al-'Arabiyya) claimed that this is from what is delayed (al-mu'akhkhar) while its meaning is advanced (al-taqdim), and the meaning of the speech according to him is: "When you seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, then recite the Qur'an." But there is no basis for what he said, because if that were the case, whenever a seeker of refuge sought refuge from the accursed Satan, it would necessarily follow that he must recite the Qur'an. Rather, its meaning is what we have described, and His saying ﴿so seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾ is not a binding command; it is rather information and recommendation (nadb). This is because there is no disagreement among all that whoever recites the Qur'an without seeking refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan, whether before his recitation or after it, has not neglected an obligatory duty. Ibn Zayd used to say something similar to what we have said.

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾: "This is an indication from Allah, the Exalted, which He has directed His servants to."

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, it means: Satan has no proof (hujja) against those who believe in Allah and His Messenger, and act upon what Allah has commanded and refrain from what Allah has forbidden them. ﴿And upon their Lord they rely﴾ means: they rely upon their Lord in the matters that befall them of their important affairs. ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾ means: his proof is only against those who worship him. ﴿And those who associate others with Him﴾ means: and those who associate others with Allah.

And according to what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿His authority is only﴾ he said: "his proof."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾, he said: "They obey him."

The people of interpretation differed regarding the reason for which Satan was not given authority over the believer.

Some of them said, as was related to me from Waqid ibn Sulayman, from Sufyan, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, he said: "He has no authority to make them commit a sin that will not be forgiven."

Others said: it is the seeking of refuge; for when one seeks refuge in Allah, he is prevented from him and is not given authority over him, and they cited as evidence for the soundness of this view the saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan comes to you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing﴾. The narration concerning that has already been mentioned in Surat al-Hijr.

Others said regarding this, with what:

al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾ up to His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: It is said that the enemy of Allah, Iblis, said ﴿I will surely mislead them all, except Your sincere servants among them﴾. So those are the ones over whom Satan has no way, and his authority is only over a people who took him as an ally and associated him in their deeds.

Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and rely upon their Lord﴾, he said: "The authority is over those who take Satan as a guardian and act in disobedience to Allah."

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying ﴿His authority is only over those who make him an ally﴾, he said: "Those who obey him and worship him."

The most correct of the interpretations regarding this is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: Indeed, he has no authority over those who believe and so seek refuge in Allah from him, by what Allah, the Exalted, has recommended of seeking refuge, ﴿and upon their Lord they rely﴾ regarding whatever thoughts and whisperings come to them.

We have said this is the most correct interpretation of the verse because Allah, the Exalted, followed this statement with ﴿So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan﴾, and He said in another place: ﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan comes to you, then seek refuge in Allah; indeed, He is Hearing, Knowing﴾. Thus it became clear that He only recommended His servants to seek refuge from Him in these circumstances in order to protect them from his authority.

As for His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, the people of interpretation differed regarding its explanation. Some of them said, in agreement with what we said, that its meaning is: and those who associate others with Allah.

Mention of those who said that:

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us; and al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, from Warqa', all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, he said: "They equate others with the Lord of the worlds."

al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾, he said: "They equate others with Allah."

I was told from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His saying ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: "They made Iblis equal to their Lord, for they are associators with Allah."

Others said: the meaning of that is: "and those who associate others with Him" means they associated Satan in their deeds.

Mention of those who said that:

al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', ﴿and those who associate others with Him﴾: "They associated him in their deeds."

The first view, namely the view of Mujahid, is the more correct of the two views regarding this, because those who take Satan as an ally only associate him with Allah in their worship, their sacrifices, their food and their drink, not that they associate Satan [with Allah as a partner]. Had the meaning of the speech been what al-Rabi' said, the wording would have been: "Those who are associators of him," and it would not have been "bihi" (with Him/with it)... so it would have been: "those who are associators of him in their deeds." Unless someone interprets the meaning of the speech to mean that the people used to hold the divinity of Satan and associate Allah with him in their worship of him, in which case the meaning of the speech would be sound, but it would depart from what the revelation brought in the rest of the Qur'an. We have not found in any part of the revelation: "Do not associate Allah with anything," nor in any part of the Qur'an, a report from Allah about them that they associated Allah with something.
