Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 101:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse, and Allah knows best what He sends down, they say, "You are only a fabricator." Rather, most of them do not know.﴾ (16:101)

Our Lord, exalted is His remembrance, says: And when We abrogate the ruling of a verse and substitute in its place another ruling, and Allah knows best what He sends down: meaning, Allah knows best what is most beneficial for His creation in what He substitutes and changes of His rulings. They say, "You are only a fabricator": meaning, the polytheists who disbelieve in Allah and deny His Messenger say to His Messenger, "You, O Muhammad, are only a fabricator," that is, a liar who invents and fabricates falsehood against Allah. Allah, exalted is He, says: Rather, most of these who say to you, O Muhammad, "You are only a fabricator," are ignorant, in that what you bring them from Allah has an abrogating and an abrogated part, and they do not know the reality of its soundness.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said things similar to what we have said in the interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse﴾.

Those who said that:

Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us. And al-Harith told me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us. And al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us. And al-Muthanna told me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, from Warqa', all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse﴾: "We lift it up and send down another in its place."

al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse﴾: He said, "We abrogated it, substituted it, lifted it up, and established another in its place."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse﴾: it is like His saying, ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten﴾ [2:106].

Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying, ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse﴾: "They say, 'You are only a fabricator'; you bring something and then revoke it, and bring something else in its place." He said: "And this substitution is abrogation, and We do not substitute a verse in place of a verse except by abrogation."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 102:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Say: The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to make firm those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims﴾ (16:102).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Say, O Muhammad, to those who say to you, "You are only a fabricator, [concerning] what you recite to them of the verses of Our Book": Say, "The Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) has brought it down." That is: Say, "Jibril has brought it from my Lord in truth." I have already explained the meaning of Ruh al-Qudus in another place, so there is no need to repeat it.

Similar to what we have said on this matter is what the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Abd al-A'la ibn Wasil narrated to me, saying: Ja'far ibn Awn al-Amari narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: "Ruh al-Qudus" is Jibril.

* *

As for His words, ﴿to make firm those who believe﴾:

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Say, "This Qur'an, its abrogating and abrogated [verses], has been brought down by the Holy Spirit from my Lord, as a means of making firm the believers and strengthening their faith, so that by their affirmation of its abrogating and abrogated [verses] they may increase in faith upon their faith, and as guidance for them away from misguidance, and as good tidings for the Muslims who submit to the command of God, yield to His command and prohibition, and to what He has sent down in the verses of His Book; so they acknowledge all of that and affirm it in word and deed."

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

The Exalted, remembered is He, says: And We know that these polytheists say, out of their ignorance, "It is only a human being from the sons of Adam who teaches Muhammad this that he recites, and it is not from God." God, exalted is His remembrance, refutes them in what they say, saying: Do you not know the falsehood of what you say? "The tongue of the one to whom you incline" means: you lean toward him, claiming that the one who teaches Muhammad is foreign-speaking. They used to claim, as has been reported, that the one who taught Muhammad this Qur'an was a Roman slave. Therefore God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ That is: this Qur'an is a clear Arabic tongue.

In accordance with what we have said, the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said, although they differed about the name of the human being whom the polytheists claimed was teaching Muhammad (ﷺ) this Qur'an. Some of them said: his name was Bal'am, and he was a smith in Makkah, a Christian.

Mention of those who said that:

Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Tahman narrated to us, from Muslim ibn 'Abd Allah al-Mala'i, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) used to teach a smith in Makkah, and he was foreign-tongued, and his name was Bal'am. The polytheists would see the Messenger of God (ﷺ) when he entered to him and when he left from his presence, and they said: "It is only Bal'am who teaches him." So God, exalted is His remembrance, revealed: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Others said: his name was Ya'ish.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib, from 'Ikrimah, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to teach a boy belonging to the Banu al-Mughirah, who was foreign-tongued. Sufyan said: I think he was called Ya'ish. He said: That is the meaning of His words: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ The Quraysh said: "It is only a human being who teaches him," a slave belonging to the Banu al-Hadrami called Ya'ish. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾ And Ya'ish used to read the books.

Others said: Rather, his name was Jabr.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ), as has reached me, would often sit near al-Marwah with a Christian boy called Jabr, a slave belonging to the Banu Bayadah al-Hadrami. They would say: "By God, Muhammad is taught most of what he brings only by Jabr, the Christian boy of the Hadrami." So God, exalted is He, revealed concerning their saying: ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him." The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir said: They used to say: "It is only a Christian at al-Marwah who teaches him," and they said Muhammad was taught by a Roman whose name they said was Jabr, who was a man of books, a slave belonging to Ibn al-Hadrami. God, exalted is He, said: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Others said: Rather, they were two boys, one named Yasar and the other Jabr.

Mention of those who said that:

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Husayn, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim al-Hadrami, that they had two slaves from the people of 'Ir al-Yemen, and they were two young boys, one of whom was called Yasar and the other Jabr. They used to read the Torah, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would sometimes sit with them. The disbelievers of Quraysh said: "He only sits with them to learn from them." So God, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ma'n ibn Asad narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Husayn, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim al-Hadrami, similarly.

Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Husayn, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim, who said: We had two boys who used to read a book of theirs in their own language, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would pass by them, stop and listen to them. The polytheists said: "He learns from them." So God, exalted is He, revealed what refutes them, saying: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

Others said: Rather, that was Salman al-Farisi.

Mention of those who said that:

It was reported to me from al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign,﴾ "They used to say: 'It is only Salman al-Farisi who teaches him.'"

Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us. And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah narrated to us, from Warqa', all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And We know that they say, "It is only a human being who teaches him."﴾ He said: The saying of the disbelievers of Quraysh was: "It is only the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami who teaches Muhammad, and he is a man of a book." God says: ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they incline is foreign, while this is a clear Arabic tongue.﴾

It was said: The one who said that was a man who wrote for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and then apostatized from Islam.

Mention of those who said that:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab informed me that the one whom God mentioned, "It is only a human being who teaches him," was tested because he used to write the revelation. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would dictate to him "Sami' 'Alim" or "'Aziz Hakim" and other endings of verses. Then the Messenger of God (ﷺ) would turn away from him while he was still on the revelation, and he would ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ), saying: "Is it 'Aziz Hakim, or Sami' 'Alim, or 'Aziz 'Alim?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) would say: "Whichever you wrote, that is how it is." This tested him, and he said: "Muhammad leaves that to me, so I write whatever I want." This is the one mentioned by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab concerning the seven ahruf (modes of recitation).

The reciters differed concerning the recitation of His words ﴿yulhidun﴾ (يُلْحِدُونَ). The majority of the reciters of Madinah and Basrah recited ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they yulhidun ilayhi﴾ with a dammah on the ya', from alhada yulhidu ilhadan, meaning they deviate, incline toward it, and turn to it, as in the words of the poet:

"Qadani min nasr al-Khubaybayn qadi... laysa amiri bil-shahih al-mulhid"

[Qadani (قَدْنِي) is a verb of sufficiency meaning "enough." Al-Khubaybayn is a diminutive dual. They are either 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr and his brother Mus'ab, or they are Khubayb ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr and one of his brothers from the sons of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, namely Hamzah, Thabit, 'Ubadah, Qays, 'Amir and Musa. It was also said that the word al-Khubaybayn is the plural of Khubayb, meaning Khubayb and those with him, or that it means the helpers of 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who was called Abu Khubayb. Al-mulhid: the author of al-Misbah said: "One who alhada fi al-haram (with the alif) is one who makes its sanctity lawful and violates it. Alhada (ألحد) means he argued and disputed. Lahada (without the alif) means he deviated and wronged." Abu 'Ubaydah said in Majaz al-Qur'an (1:368): "'The tongue of the one to whom they yulhidun is foreign' means they turn toward it. It is said: alhada fulan, meaning he deviated." A'jami (أعجمي) is attributed to a' jam al-lisan (one whose tongue is non-Arab). The two verses are from the rajaz meter, and they belong to Humayd al-Arqat (see Khizanat al-Baghdadi 2:453).]

The reciters of Kufah, most of them, recited ﴿The tongue of the one to whom they yalhidun ilayhi﴾ with a fathah on the ya', meaning they incline toward it, from lahada fulan ila hadha al-amr, yalhadu lahadan and lahudan. In my view these are two dialects with one meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads is correct in both.

It was also said that ﴿And this is a clear Arabic tongue﴾ means the Qur'an, just as the Arabs say of a poem that a poet presents: "This is the tongue of so-and-so," meaning his poem, as the poet said:

"Lisan al-su' tuhdiha ilayna... wa hinta wa ma hasibtuka an tahinna..."

meaning by "tongue" the poem and the word. [In (Lisan: L-S-N): al-lisan is the organ of speech, and it is sometimes used metonymically for the word, in which case it is feminine. A'sha Bahilah said: "Inni 'atatni lisan la asurru biha." Ibn Barri said: here al-lisan means the message and the statement. It may also be used in the sense of speech; al-Hutay'ah said: "Nadimtu 'ala lisan fat minni." Hana yahin hinan means he perished. The author's proof in the verse is that lisan may "perish," being feminine in the sense of word and poem.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 104–106:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah – Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment. (104) It is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood, and those are the liars. (105)﴾

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed, those who do not believe in the proofs and evidences of Allah, so they do not affirm what they indicate, ﴿Allah will not guide them﴾, meaning: Allah will not grant them success in reaching the truth, nor will He guide them to the path of rectitude in this world. And for them in the Hereafter, and before Allah when they come to Him on the Day of Resurrection, is a painful, agonizing punishment. Then He, the Exalted and Remembered, informed about the polytheists who said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "You are only a fabricator", that it is they who are the people of slander and lying, not the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) and those who believe in him. And He cleared His Prophet (ﷺ) and his Companions of that, so He said: It is only those who fabricate lies and invent falsehood, those who do not affirm the proofs of Allah and His announcements, because they do not hope for reward for truthfulness, and do not fear punishment for lying, who are the people of falsehood and fabricated lies, not one who hopes from Allah for abundant reward for truthfulness and fears a painful punishment for lying.

* *

And His saying ﴿and those are the liars﴾

He says: Those who do not believe in the signs of Allah are the people of lying, not the believers.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief – except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith – but those who open their breasts to disbelief – upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment. (106)﴾

The grammarians (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the governing element (al-'amil) of "man" (مَنْ) in His saying ﴿man kafara billah (whoever disbelieves in Allah)﴾ and in His saying ﴿wa-lakin man sharaha bil-kufri sadran (but those who open their breasts to disbelief)﴾. Some of the grammarians of Basra said: His saying ﴿fa-'alayhim (upon them)﴾ became the predicate of His saying ﴿wa-lakin man sharaha bil-kufri sadran﴾, and His saying ﴿man kafara billahi min ba'di imanihi (whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief)﴾ is informed of with one predicate for both, and this indicates the meaning. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: These are two conditional clauses that have come together, the second dependent on the first, so their response is one, like the speaker's saying: "Whoever comes to us, whoever is good, we honor him," meaning: whoever among those who come to us is good, we honor him. He said: Likewise every two conditionals that have come together, the second dependent on the first, so the response to both is one. Another of the grammarians of Basra said: Rather, His saying ﴿man kafara billah﴾ is in the nominative by way of resumption (al-radd) upon those in His saying ﴿Indeed, it is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood﴾, and the meaning of the statement in his view is: It is only the one who disbelieves in Allah after his belief who invents falsehood, except one of these who is forced while his heart is firm in faith. This is a view without basis. That is because if the meaning of the statement were as the proponent of this view said, Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, would have excluded from those who invent falsehood in this verse those who were born upon disbelief and persisted in it and never believed, and He would have singled out for it those who had believed at one time and then returned to disbelief after belief. The revelation indicates that He did not single out these over the rest of the polytheists who remained upon polytheism. That is because He, the Exalted, informed about a group of them who attributed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the fabrication of lies, so He said: ﴿And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse – and Allah knows best what He sends down – they say, "You are only a fabricator." But most of them do not know.﴾ And He denied all the polytheists for their fabrication against Allah, and informed that they are more deserving of this description than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so He said: ﴿It is only those who do not believe in the signs of Allah who invent falsehood, and those are the liars.﴾ And if those meant by this verse were those who disbelieved in Allah after their belief, it would necessarily follow that those who said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), "You are only a fabricator," when Allah substituted a verse for a verse, were specifically those who disbelieved in Allah after belief and no others of the rest of the polytheists, because this is in the context of the report about them. And that is a view which, if someone holds it, its corruption is evident, along with its departure from the interpretation of all the people of knowledge of interpretation.

The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is that the element that makes "man" in the first and second instances nominative is His saying ﴿fa-'alayhim ghadabun min Allah (upon them is wrath from Allah)﴾, and the Arabs do this with conditional particles when they begin one of them after another.

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir and a people who had embraced Islam, whom the polytheists tempted away from their religion; some of them remained steadfast in Islam, and some of them succumbed to temptation.

Mention of those who said so:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾ ... to the end of the verse. That was because the polytheists seized 'Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him, then left him. He returned to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and told him of what he had met from the Quraysh, and what he had said. So Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, revealed his excuse: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and for them is a great punishment.﴾

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾ He said: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, whom the Banu al-Mughira seized and dipped into the well of Maymun, and they said: "Disbelieve in Muhammad." So he complied with them in that while his heart was averse. So Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, revealed: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith. But those who open their breasts to disbelief﴾: that is, whoever came to disbelief by choice and preference, ﴿upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn Yasir, he said: The polytheists seized 'Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him until he gave them some of what they wanted. He complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How do you find your heart?" He said: "Firm in faith." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If they return, then return."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, concerning His saying ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When al-A'bad were tortured, they gave them what they asked for, except Khabbab ibn al-Aratt; they used to lay him on hot stones, and they could not get anything from him.

So the interpretation of the statement is therefore: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who is forced to disbelief, so that he utters the word of disbelief with his tongue while his heart remains firm in faith, certain of its reality, his resolve sound upon it, and his breast not opened to disbelief. But whoever opens his breast to disbelief, choosing it and preferring it over faith, and declaring it willingly, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.

The report has come with what we have said on this matter, from Ibn 'Abbas.

⁕ Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾: Allah, glorified is He, informed that whoever disbelieves after his belief, upon him is wrath from Allah and for him is a great punishment. As for one who is forced and utters it with his tongue while his heart contradicts it with faith, so that he may be saved thereby from his enemy, there is no blame upon him, because Allah, glorified is He, only holds His servants accountable for what their hearts have committed to.

So Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, revealed his excuse: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief﴾ ... to His saying ﴿and for them is a great punishment.﴾

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾ He said: It was mentioned to us that it was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir, whom the Banu al-Mughira seized and dipped into the well of Maymun, and they said: "Disbelieve in Muhammad." So he complied with them in that while his heart was averse. So Allah, the Exalted and Remembered, revealed: ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith. But those who open their breasts to disbelief﴾: that is, whoever came to disbelief by choice and preference, ﴿upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.﴾

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Abu 'Ubaydah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn Yasir, he said: The polytheists seized 'Ammar ibn Yasir and tortured him until he gave them some of what they wanted. He complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "How do you find your heart?" He said: "Firm in faith." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "If they return, then return."

⁕ Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, concerning His saying ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾, he said: It was revealed concerning 'Ammar ibn Yasir.

⁕ Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, who said: When al-A'bad were tortured, they gave them what they asked for, except Khabbab ibn al-Aratt; they used to lay him on hot stones, and they could not get anything from him.

So the interpretation of the statement is therefore: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who is forced to disbelief, so that he utters the word of disbelief with his tongue while his heart remains firm in faith, certain of its reality, his resolve sound upon it, and his breast not opened to disbelief. But whoever opens his breast to disbelief, choosing it and preferring it over faith, and declaring it willingly, upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment.

The report has come with what we have said on this matter, from Ibn 'Abbas.

⁕ Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, he said: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying ﴿except one who has been forced while his heart remains firm in faith﴾: Allah, glorified is He, informed that whoever disbelieves after his belief, upon him is wrath from Allah and for him is a great punishment. As for one who is forced and utters it with his tongue while his heart contradicts it with faith, so that he may be saved thereby from his enemy, there is no blame upon him, because Allah, glorified is He, only holds His servants accountable for what their hearts have committed to.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 16, verses 107–109:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and because Allah does not guide the disbelieving people﴾ (107)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: The wrath of Allah has descended upon these polytheists, and the great punishment has become binding upon them, because they chose the adornment of the life of this world over the bliss of the Hereafter, and because Allah does not grant success to the people who deny His signs while persisting in their denial.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, words: ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts, hearing and sight Allah has sealed, and those are the heedless﴾ (108) ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers﴾ (109)

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: These polytheists whose description I have given you in these verses, O people, are the folk whom Allah has sealed upon their hearts, stamping them with His seal, so they do not believe nor are guided; and He has made their ears deaf so they do not hear the call of Allah to guidance, and blinded their eyes so they do not see the proofs of Allah with the sight of one who takes heed and admonishes himself. ﴿And those are the heedless﴾ means: and those upon whom Allah has placed these acts are the unmindful, unaware of what Allah has prepared for the likes of them among the people of disbelief, and of what is intended for them.

* *

As for His words ﴿Certainly, in the Hereafter they will be the greatest losers﴾:

They are the doomed, who have cheated themselves of their portion of Allah's honour.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 110:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, words: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says: Then indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is for those who emigrated from their homes, their dwellings and their tribes among the polytheists, and moved away from them to the lands and dwellings of the people of Islam and the people of their allegiance, after the polytheists who were among them before their emigration tested them concerning their religion. Then they struggled against the polytheists afterwards, with their hands by the sword and with their tongues by disavowing them and what they worship besides Allah, and they were patient in their struggle. ﴿Indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ He says: indeed your Lord, after their act, is forgiving toward them, meaning: possessor of concealment regarding what they did in giving the polytheists what they wanted from them, a word of disbelief with their tongues, while they were concealing other than it and holding faith in their hearts; and He is merciful to them, not punishing them for it, given their turning back to Allah and their repentance.

It has been mentioned from some of the people of interpretation that this verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had remained behind in Mecca after the Prophet's ﷺ emigration. The polytheists pressed hard upon them until they tested them away from their religion, so they despaired of repentance, and Allah revealed this verse concerning them: they emigrated and joined the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

Those who said this: Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who is forced while his heart is at rest with faith﴾, he said: some people of Mecca had become Muslim, and some of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ in Medina wrote to them that they should emigrate, "for we do not consider you of us until you emigrate to us." So they set out seeking Medina, but the Quraysh overtook them on the road, tested them, and they disbelieved under compulsion; concerning them this verse was revealed.

⁕ Al-Qasim related to me, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly.

Ibn Juraij said: Allah, may He be remembered and exalted, said: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief﴾, then abrogated and made an exception, saying: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾: it was mentioned to us that when Allah revealed that Islam of the people of Mecca would not be accepted until they emigrated, the people of Medina wrote this to their companions among the people of Mecca; when that reached them, they pledged among themselves to set out, and if the polytheists of Mecca pursued them, they would fight them until they were saved or joined Allah. They set out, the polytheists overtook them and fought them; some of them were killed and some were saved. Then Allah, exalted, revealed ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested﴾ ... the verse.

⁕ Ahmad ibn Mansur related to us, saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Shurayk related to us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: some people of Mecca had become Muslim, and they used to conceal their Islam. The polytheists took them out with them on the day of Badr; some of them were struck and some were killed. The Muslims said: "These companions of ours were Muslims, but they were compelled, so ask forgiveness for them." Then ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves﴾ ... to the end of the verse was revealed. He said: this verse was written to those Muslims who remained in Mecca, that they had no excuse. He said: so they set out, the polytheists overtook them and inflicted the trial upon them, and then ﴿And among the people is he who says, "We believe in Allah," but when he is harmed for the cause of Allah, he regards the trial of people as like the punishment of Allah﴾ ... to the end of the verse was revealed. The Muslims wrote this to them, so they set out, and they despaired of all good. Then ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ was revealed concerning them. They were written to with this: "Indeed Allah has made a way out for you," so they set out; the polytheists overtook them and fought them; then whoever was saved was saved, and whoever was killed was killed.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: this verse was revealed concerning Ammar ibn Yasir, Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a, and al-Walid ibn al-Walid: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient﴾.

Others said: rather, this verse was revealed concerning the matter of Ibn Abi Sarh.

Those who said this:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said regarding Surat al-Nahl: ﴿Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief, except one who is forced while his heart is at rest with faith; but whoever opens his breast to disbelief — upon them is wrath from Allah, and for them is a great punishment﴾. Then He abrogated and made an exception from that, saying ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they had been tested, then struggled and were patient — indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. This refers to Abdullah ibn Abi Sarh, who used to write for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; Satan made him slip, so he joined the disbelievers. The Prophet ﷺ commanded that he be killed on the day of the Conquest of Mecca, but Abu Amr [[Abu Amr: he means Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah have mercy on him, who was a milk-brother of Abdullah ibn Sa'd, as Ibn Ishaq stated in the Sira.]] sought protection for him, and the Prophet ﷺ granted him protection.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 111:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day when every soul will come pleading for itself, and every soul will be paid in full for what it has done, and they will not be wronged﴾ (16:111).

He, exalted is His remembrance, says: Indeed your Lord, after these (trials), is Forgiving and Merciful. ﴿On the Day when every soul comes﴾ disputing on its own behalf, and pleading on its own behalf with what it had sent forward in the world of good or evil, or faith or disbelief. ﴿And every soul will be paid in full for what it has done﴾ in the world, of obedience and disobedience. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: that is, nothing will be done to them except what they deserve and merit by what they sent forward of good or evil. The good-doer will not be recompensed except with goodness, and the evildoer will not be recompensed except with what he sent forward of evil. No one who does good will be punished, nor will the reward of his goodness be diminished, and no evildoer will be rewarded except with the reward of his deed.

The scholars of Arabic grammar (ahl al-'arabiyya) differed regarding the reason why ﴿tujadilu﴾ (pleads) was said and the feminine form was used with ﴿kull﴾ (every). Some grammarians of Basra said: It was said this way because the meaning of ﴿kull nafs﴾ (every soul) is "every person," and the feminine was used because nafs may be masculine or feminine; it is said: "No single person (nafs wahid) and no single woman (nafs wahida) came to me." But some of the grammarians held that this view of its proponent was an error, and said: When ﴿kull﴾ is added to a singular indefinite noun, the verb follows the form of that noun: kullu imra'atin qa'imatun (every woman is standing), kullu rajulin qa'imun (every man is standing), kullu imra'atayni qa'imatani (every two women are standing), kullu rajulayni qa'imani (every two men are standing), kullu nisa'in qa'imatun (every group of women are standing), kullu rijalin qa'imun (every group of men are standing). Thus the verb follows the number, feminine and masculine of the indefinite noun, and there is no need to make nafs feminine or masculine.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 112:

The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And Allah presents a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place. But it denied the favours of Allah, so Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear for what they used to do.﴾

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: And Allah struck a parable for Makkah, the town whose inhabitants were people of polytheism toward Allah, namely the town that was secure and tranquil. Its security was that the Arabs were at enmity with one another, killing and taking captives from among themselves, while the people of Makkah were not raided and were not attacked in their own land. That was its security.

* *

As for His saying ﴿tranquil﴾:

That is, settled with its inhabitants, whose people do not need to move about in search of pasture, as the dwellers of the desert needed to. ﴿Its provision coming to it abundantly﴾ means: its means of livelihood come to its people in abundance and plenty.

* *

As for His saying ﴿from every place﴾:

That is, from every mountain pass of this town and from every direction within it.

Concerning the view we have stated, that the town mentioned in this passage is intended to be Makkah, the people of interpretation have said:

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying (And Allah struck a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place): he meant Makkah.

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, he said: 'Isa narrated to us. And al-Harith narrated to me, he said: al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, ﴿a town that was secure and tranquil﴾, he said: Makkah.

⁕ al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿And Allah struck a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil﴾, he said: It was mentioned to us that it is Makkah.

⁕ Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, ﴿a town that was secure﴾, he said: It is Makkah.

⁕ Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying ﴿And Allah struck a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil﴾ ... to the end of the verse. He said: This is Makkah.

Others said: Rather, the town mentioned by Allah in this passage is the city of the Messenger ﷺ (Madinah).

Those who said this:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi narrated to me, he said: Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, he said: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayh narrated to me, that 'Abd al-Karim ibn al-Harith al-Hadrami related that he heard Mishrah ibn 'Ahan say: I heard Sulaym ibn Numayr say: We returned from the Hajj with Hafsah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, while 'Uthman was besieged in Madinah. She kept asking about him, what had happened to him, until she saw two riders. She sent to them asking them, and they said: He has been killed. Hafsah said: By Him in whose hand my soul is, it is the town, meaning Madinah, of which Allah, the Exalted, said ﴿And Allah struck a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil, its provision coming to it abundantly from every place, but it denied the favours of Allah﴾, she recited it. Abu Shurayh said: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah informed me, from one who narrated to him, that he used to say: It is Madinah. As for His saying ﴿but it denied the favours of Allah﴾, it means: the people of this town denied the favours of Allah which He bestowed upon them.

The grammarians differed concerning the singular of al-an'um (favours). Some of the grammarians of Basra said: al-an'um is the plural of al-ni'mah (favour), as in Allah's saying ﴿until he reached his maturity (ashuddah)﴾, which he took to be the plural of shiddah (strength). Another of them said the singular is nu'm, and said: it is said: ayyam ta'm wa-na'm, meaning days of pleasure (na'im). He said: So it is permissible that its meaning be: they denied the pleasure of Allah for them. He cited in support of this the verse of the poet:

"And with me are the reserves of good and evil, all of it, so woe to the one who is in woe, and favour with favours."

[[In Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah (1:369) at the verse: its singular is "ni'm", with the nun vowelled and the 'ayn quiescent, and its meaning is ni'mah (favour), and they are one. They said: the herald of the Prophet ﷺ proclaimed at Mina: "These are days of food and favour, so do not fast." In al-Lisan: ni'm; and the plural of ni'mah is ni'm and an'um, like shiddah and ashudd, as transmitted by Sibawayh. And al-Nabighah said: "So I shall never mention al-Nu'man except with goodness, for he has for me a favour (yad) and favours (an'um)." And al-ni'm is the opposite of bu's (misery). It is said: a day of ni'm and a day of bu's. The plural is an'um and abu's.]]

Some of the people of Kufa said: an'um is the plural of ni'ma', like ba'sa' and ab'us, and dara' and adarr; as for ashudd, he claimed it is the plural of shadd.

* *

As for His saying ﴿So Allah made it taste the garment of hunger and fear﴾:

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Allah made the people of this town taste the garment of hunger, which was a hunger whose harm permeated their bodies, so Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, made it, because it penetrated their bodies, like a garment for them. This is because hunger was imposed upon them for successive years through the supplication of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until they ate al-'ilhiz and carrion. Abu Ja'far said: al-'ilhiz is the hair of camels kneaded with blood, which they ate, and ticks; as for fear, it was their fear of the expeditions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which encircled them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿for what they used to do﴾:

That is: for what they used to do of disbelief in the favours of Allah, denying His signs and calling His Messenger a liar. He said: "for what they used to do," although the discourse from the beginning of the verse to this point has proceeded in the form of a report about the town. For although the report ran in speech about the town, by mentioning it they dispensed with mentioning its people, since the listeners knew what was meant by it; the intended meaning is its people, and therefore it was said ﴿for what they used to do﴾, returning the report to the people of the town. This is like His saying ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it by night or while they were napping﴾, where He did not say "napping" (a feminine form), and He had said before it ﴿Then Our punishment came upon it﴾, because He returned the report to the account of the people of the town. Similar instances in the Qur'an are numerous.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ (113)**

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: And there had certainly come to the people of this town, whose description God gave in the verse before this verse, ﴿a messenger from among themselves﴾. That is, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was from among them; that is, from their own selves, they knew him, they knew his lineage and the truthfulness of his speech, and he called them to the truth and to a straight path. ﴿But they denied him﴾, and did not accept what he brought them from God. ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, and that was the garment of hunger and fear in place of security and tranquility and the abundant provision they had been receiving before that, and they were killed by the sword. ﴿While they were wrongdoers﴾: that is, they were polytheists, and that is because their leaders were killed by the sword on the Day of Badr for their polytheism.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves﴾: Yes, by God, they knew his lineage and his affair. ﴿But they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾: so God seized them with hunger, fear and killing.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good, and be grateful for the favor of God, if it is Him you worship (114)﴾**

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: So eat, O people, of what God has provided for you from the grazing livestock, which He made lawful for you, [as] lawful and good, slaughtered properly, not forbidden to you. ﴿And be grateful for the favor of God﴾: that is, be thankful to God for His favors which He bestowed upon you in making lawful for you what He has made lawful of that, and for His other favors. ﴿If it is Him you worship﴾: that is, if you worship God, obeying Him in what He commands and forbids you.

Some of them said: By His words ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good﴾ He meant food which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to the polytheists of his people in years of drought and famine, out of compassion for them, and God, the Exalted, said to the polytheists: So eat of what God has provided for you from this which he sent to you, [as] lawful and good. But that is a far-fetched interpretation from what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because God, the Exalted, has followed that with His words: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood...﴾ ... the verse and what follows it, thereby making clear that His words ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good﴾ are God's informing His servants that what the polytheists used to forbid of the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and other things we have already explained earlier, has no basis, since all of that is from the footsteps of Satan; for all of that is lawful, and God has not forbidden any of it.

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾ (113)**

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: And there had certainly come to the people of this town, whose description God gave in the verse before this verse, ﴿a messenger from among themselves﴾. That is, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was from among them; that is, from their own selves, they knew him, they knew his lineage and the truthfulness of his speech, and he called them to the truth and to a straight path. ﴿But they denied him﴾, and did not accept what he brought them from God. ﴿So the punishment seized them﴾, and that was the garment of hunger and fear in place of security and tranquility and the abundant provision they had been receiving before that, and they were killed by the sword. ﴿While they were wrongdoers﴾: that is, they were polytheists, and that is because their leaders were killed by the sword on the Day of Badr for their polytheism.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Mention of those who said that:

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿And there had certainly come to them a messenger from among themselves﴾: Yes, by God, they knew his lineage and his affair. ﴿But they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers﴾: so God seized them with hunger, fear and killing.

* *

**The interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good, and be grateful for the favor of God, if it is Him you worship (114)﴾**

God, His remembrance is exalted, says: So eat, O people, of what God has provided for you from the grazing livestock, which He made lawful for you, [as] lawful and good, slaughtered properly, not forbidden to you. ﴿And be grateful for the favor of God﴾: that is, be thankful to God for His favors which He bestowed upon you in making lawful for you what He has made lawful of that, and for His other favors. ﴿If it is Him you worship﴾: that is, if you worship God, obeying Him in what He commands and forbids you.

Some of them said: By His words ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good﴾ He meant food which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sent to the polytheists of his people in years of drought and famine, out of compassion for them, and God, the Exalted, said to the polytheists: So eat of what God has provided for you from this which he sent to you, [as] lawful and good. But that is a far-fetched interpretation from what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates, because God, the Exalted, has followed that with His words: ﴿He has only forbidden you carrion, blood...﴾ ... the verse and what follows it, thereby making clear that His words ﴿So eat of what God has provided for you [as] lawful and good﴾ are God's informing His servants that what the polytheists used to forbid of the baheerah, the saa'ibah, the waseelah, and other things we have already explained earlier, has no basis, since all of that is from the footsteps of Satan; for all of that is lawful, and God has not forbidden any of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 115:

The interpretation of His, may He be exalted, saying: ﴿Indeed, He has forbidden you only dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (115)

He, may He be exalted and remembered, says, refuting the polytheists who used to forbid what we have mentioned of the baḥā'ir (slit-eared she-camels) and other things: "Allah has forbidden you, O people, only dead animals, blood, and the flesh of swine, and that which is slaughtered for idols (anṣāb), over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, because that is the slaughter of those whose slaughtered animals are not lawful to eat. Whoever is compelled to that, or to some part of it, by hunger, it becomes lawful for him, and he eats it ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾." He says: He is Concealing, so He does not hold him to account for eating that in a state of necessity, and Merciful toward him, so that He does not punish him for it.

We have already explained the differences of the scholars regarding His saying ﴿neither desiring nor transgressing﴾, and the correct view in our opinion on that matter, with its evidences, has been set forth earlier in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary.

⁕ Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying ﴿Indeed, He has forbidden you only dead animals and blood﴾ ... the verse. He said: "Indeed, Islam is a religion which Allah purifies from every evil, and He has made for you, O son of Adam, a provision therein when you are compelled to something of that."

* *

Regarding His saying ﴿but whoever is forced, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾:

"Neither desiring" in eating it, "nor transgressing" by going beyond the lawful to the unlawful while he has an alternative to it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 116–117:

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And do not say, concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful," to invent lies against Allah. Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed. A brief enjoyment, and for them is a painful punishment.﴾

The reciters differed over the reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz and Iraq read ﴿وَلا تَقُولُوا لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكَذِبَ﴾ (wa-la taqulu lima tasifu alsinatukumu al-kadhiba), so that "tasifu" governs "al-kadhiba," meaning: "Do not say, for the description your tongues make, the lie," so that "mā" (ما) is in the sense of a verbal noun (maṣdar). It is reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he read ﴿الْكَذِبِ﴾ with the genitive (khafḍ) on al-kadhib, meaning: "Do not say, to the lie which your tongues describe," so that al-kadhib is treated as an apposition to the "mā" in lima, and it takes the case that "mā" takes. It has also been related from some of them: ﴿لِمَا تَصِفُ أَلْسِنَتُكُمُ الْكُذُبُ﴾ with the nominative (raf') on al-kudhub, making al-kudhub a description of the tongues, and it is read on the pattern fu'ul, as a plural of kadhub and kadhib, like shukur and shukr.

The correct reading in my view is the accusative of al-kadhib, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters upon it. Thus the meaning of the speech, given that this is so for the reason we have mentioned, is: "Do not say, for the description your tongues make of the lie concerning what Allah has granted His servants of foods, 'This is lawful and this is unlawful,' so that you invent lies against Allah by your saying that. For Allah has not forbidden what you forbid from that, nor has He made lawful much of what you make lawful." Then He warned them of their lying against Him, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who invent lies against Allah will not succeed﴾, meaning: indeed those who fabricate and invent falsehood against Allah will not be made to abide in this world, nor will they remain in it; they will only enjoy it for a little while. He said ﴿A brief enjoyment﴾ in the nominative, because the state they are in from this world is a brief enjoyment, or: for them is a brief enjoyment in this world.

* *

As for His words ﴿and for them is a painful punishment﴾:

This means: then to Us is their return and their final destination, and for them, because of their lying and their fabrication against Allah, is a painful punishment upon their arrival at Him.

The exegetes have said what is similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa related to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of Allah, exalted is He, ﴿concerning what your tongues describe falsely, "This is lawful and this is unlawful"﴾: concerning the baheera and the saiba.

Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, who said: the baha'ir and the sawa'ib.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, the Exalted: ﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited what We had related to you before; and We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.﴾ (16:118)

He, the Exalted and Mighty, says: And We prohibited, O Muhammad, upon the Jews, before this, what We had informed you of in Surah al-An'am, namely every animal with claws, and from the cattle and the sheep We prohibited for them their fat, except what their backs carried or the entrails (al-hawaya), or what was mixed with bone. ﴿And We did not wrong them﴾ by Our prohibiting that for them, ﴿but they were wronging themselves﴾, so We recompensed them for that with their transgression against their Lord and their wronging of themselves by disobeying God, and that brought upon them the punishment of God.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) said the same as what we have said concerning this.

Mention of those who said that:

Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited what We had related to you before﴾, he said: "In Surah al-An'am."

Yaqub related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ayyub, from 'Ikrimah, concerning His words ﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited what We had related to you before﴾, he said: "In Surah al-An'am."

Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited what We had related to you before﴾, he said: "What God, the Exalted, related in Surah al-An'am, where He says ﴿And upon those who were Jews We prohibited every animal with claws﴾ ... the verse."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 119:

The explanation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Then indeed your Lord, for those who did evil in ignorance and then repented after that and reformed, indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (16:119).

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Indeed your Lord is for those who disobeyed Allah, acting ignorantly by their committing what they committed of disobedience to Allah, and acting foolishly thereby, then they returned to the obedience of Allah and to regret over it, and to seeking forgiveness and repenting from it, after what had passed of them of committing disobedience, and [they] reformed, acting in accordance with what Allah loves and is pleased with. ﴿Indeed your Lord, after that﴾ means: indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, after their repentance to Him, ﴿is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verses 120–121:

The explanation of His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah. (120) Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path.﴾ (121)

He, the Exalted, says: Indeed Abraham, the friend of Allah (khalil Allah), was a teacher of good, whom the people of guidance follow. ﴿Qanitan﴾ means obedient to Allah. ﴿Hanifan﴾ means steadfast upon the religion of Islam. ﴿And he was not of those who associate others with Allah﴾ means: he did not associate anything with Allah, so as to be among the allies of those who associate others with Him. This is a declaration from Allah, the Exalted, to the polytheists of Quraysh that Abraham is innocent of them and they are innocent of him. ﴿Grateful for His favors﴾ means: he sincerely gave thanks to Allah for the blessings He bestowed upon him, and did not make any partner with Him in his thanks for His favors, such as idols, rivals, or anything else, as the polytheists of Quraysh do. ﴿He chose him﴾ means: He selected him and chose him for His friendship (khullah). ﴿And guided him to a straight path﴾ means: He directed him to the right path, which is the religion of Islam, not Judaism nor Christianity.

Ahl al-ta'wil (the scholars of interpretation) said things in agreement with what we have said regarding the meaning of ﴿a nation, devoutly obedient﴾.

Mention of those who said that:

* Zakariyya ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from al-Hakam, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn, that he came to 'Abd Allah (ibn Mas'ud) and said: "Whom shall we ask if we do not ask you?" So Ibn Mas'ud took pity on him and said: "Tell me about the ummah." He said: "The one who teaches people good."

* Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Kuhayl, from Muslim al-Batin, from Abu al-'Ubaydayn, that he asked 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud about the devoutly obedient ummah. He said: "The ummah is the teacher of good, and the qanit is the one obedient to Allah and His Messenger."

* Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Mansur, meaning Ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Farwa ibn Nawfal al-Ashja'i narrated to me, saying: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth." I said to myself: "Abu 'Abd al-Rahman has erred; Allah the Exalted only said ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾." He said: "Do you know what the ummah is, and what the qanit is?" I said: "Allah knows best." He said: "The ummah is the one who teaches good, and the qanit is the one obedient to Allah and His Messenger. And thus Mu'adh ibn Jabal used to teach good, and he was obedient to Allah and His Messenger."

* Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Firas narrate, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah." He said: A man from Ashja' called Farwa ibn Nawfal said: "He forgot; rather, that was Abraham." 'Abd Allah said: "Whoever forgot, we used to liken him to Abraham." He said: 'Abd Allah was asked about the ummah, and he said: "The teacher of good, and the qanit is the one obedient to Allah and His Messenger."

* Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I recited this verse in the presence of 'Abd Allah: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾." He said: "Mu'adh was a devoutly obedient nation." He said: "Do you know what the ummah is? The ummah is the one who teaches people good, and the qanit is the one who obeys Allah and His Messenger."

* Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: Bayan ibn Bishr al-Bajali narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: 'Abd Allah said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of the polytheists." A man said to him: "You have forgotten." He said: "No, but he resembled Abraham. The ummah is the teacher of good, and the qanit is the obedient."

* 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Kindi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from al-Sha'bi, concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, inclining toward truth﴾ he said: "Obedient."

* Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a devoutly obedient nation, a teacher of good."

Various things have been mentioned about the word ummah on which people differ: He said ﴿and remembered after a period (ummah)﴾, meaning: after a time; and ﴿a middle nation (ummah wasatan)﴾.

* Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Sabiq, from Layth, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "The earth has never been without fourteen by whom Allah repels (harm) from the people of the earth and its blessings are brought forth, except in the time of Abraham, for he was alone."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Sayyar informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Zakariyya and Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud, similar to the report of Ya'qub, from Ibn 'Ulayyah, and he added in it: "The ummah is the one who teaches good and is followed and imitated; and the qanit is the one obedient to Allah and to the Messenger." Abu Farwa al-Kindi said to him: "You have erred."

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾ as a separate word, ﴿devoutly obedient to Allah﴾: he said: "Obedient."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "Obedient to Allah in this world."

Ibn Juraij said: Uwaymir informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: "Qanitan: obedient."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾, he said: "He was a leader of guidance, obedient, whose sunnah and religion are followed."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a devoutly obedient nation." Other than Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Do you know what the ummah is? The one who teaches good."

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I recited in the presence of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient﴾." He said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a devoutly obedient nation." He said: They repeated it, so he repeated it to them, then said: "Do you know what the ummah is? The one who teaches people good, and the qanit is the one who obeys Allah."

We have already explained the meaning of ummah and its aspects, and the meaning of qanit, with the differing views of those who differ concerning it, in another place in our book with their evidences, so this is sufficient without repeating it here.

* Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all of them, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation﴾ as a separate word, ﴿devoutly obedient to Allah﴾: he said: "Obedient."

* al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, similarly, except that he said: "Obedient to Allah in this world."

Ibn Juraij said: Uwaymir informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he said: "Qanitan: obedient."

* Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah﴾, he said: "He was a leader of guidance, obedient, whose sunnah and religion are followed."

* Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, that Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed Mu'adh ibn Jabal was a devoutly obedient nation." Other than Qatadah said: Ibn Mas'ud said: "Do you know what the ummah is? The one who teaches good."

* al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, who said: "I recited in the presence of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient﴾." He said: "Indeed Mu'adh was a devoutly obedient nation." He said: They repeated it, so he repeated it to them, then said: "Do you know what the ummah is? The one who teaches people good, and the qanit is the one who obeys Allah."

We have already explained the meaning of ummah and its aspects, and the meaning of qanit, with the differing views of those who differ concerning it, in another place in our book with their evidences, so this is sufficient without repeating it here.
