The explanation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and argue with them in the way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of those who are guided.﴾ (16:125)

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): ﴿Call⁠﴾, O Muhammad, to whom your Lord has sent you, by calling them to obey Him. ﴿to the way of your Lord﴾: that is, to the law of your Lord which He has prescribed for His creation, and it is Islam. ﴿with wisdom﴾: that is, by the revelation of God which He reveals to you and the Book which He sends down to you. ﴿and good admonition﴾: that is, with the fine lessons which God made a proof against them in His Book, and reminded them of in His revelation, like those proofs of His that He enumerated to them in this surah, and the favors of His that He reminded them of in it. ﴿and argue with them in the way that is best﴾: that is, dispute with them in the manner that is better than other manners, by overlooking the harm they have inflicted upon your honor, and do not fall short in carrying out the duty incumbent upon you of conveying the message of your Lord.

And the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said something similar to what we have said regarding this.

Mention of those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, saying: 'Isa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God: ﴿and argue with them in the way that is best﴾: "Turn away from their harm to you."

⁕ al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way﴾

He, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Indeed your Lord, O Muhammad, is most knowing of those who have deviated from the straight path among those who differed concerning the Sabbath and other matters among His creation, and who opposed God; and He is most knowing of those among them who were following the straight path and the highway of truth. And He will recompense all of them with their due reward when they come before Him.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient.﴾ (16:126)

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to the believers: "And if you, O believers, punish those who wronged you and transgressed against you, then punish him with the like of the punishment that your wrongdoer inflicted upon you. And if you are patient in refraining from punishing him, and you seek reward from Allah for the wrong that befell you, and you entrust his matter to Him, so that He Himself is the one who takes vengeance on him, ﴿it is indeed better for the patient﴾." He says: refraining from punishing him in this way is better for those who are patient, seeking reward from Allah, because Allah will compensate them for what they wished to obtain by taking revenge on their wrongdoer for his wrong against them, namely the pleasure of victory. The pronoun in ﴿it [lahuwa]﴾ refers to patience, and its reference is acceptable even though patience was not mentioned before it, because of the indication of His saying ﴿and if you are patient﴾.

The people of interpretation have differed regarding the occasion on which this verse was revealed, and regarding whether it is abrogated (mansukh) or definitive (muhkam). Some of them said: it was revealed because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions swore, when the polytheists did to the slain Muslims at the Battle of Uhud what they did, including mutilating them, that they would exceed what they had done in mutilating them if they were ever granted victory over them one day. So Allah forbade them from that by this verse, and commanded them that if they gained victory over them, they should limit their mutilation to the like of what had been done to them. Then He commanded them afterward to abandon mutilation and to prefer patience in refraining from it, by His saying ﴿But be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah﴾. Thus, according to them, what He had permitted them of mutilation was abrogated.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Dawud, from ʿAmir: that when the Muslims saw what the polytheists did to their slain at Uhud, they said: "If we gain the upper hand over them, we will certainly do the like, and do the like!" So Allah, the Exalted, revealed ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient.﴾ They said: "Rather, we will be patient."

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿAmir, who said: When the Muslims saw what the polytheists did to their slain at Uhud, of ripping open the bellies, cutting off the private parts, and the evil mutilation, they said: "If Allah grants us victory over them, we will certainly do the like, and do the like!" So Allah revealed concerning them ﴿But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient. And be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah.﴾

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from some of his companions, from ʿAtaʾ ibn Yasar, who said: The whole of Surat an-Nahl was revealed at Mecca, and it is Meccan, except for three verses at its end, which were revealed at Medina after Uhud, when Hamza was killed and mutilated. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If we gain the upper hand over them, we will mutilate thirty men of them." When the Muslims heard that, they said: "By Allah, if we gain the upper hand over them, we will mutilate them with a mutilation that no Arab has ever inflicted upon anyone." So Allah revealed ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient﴾ ... to the end of the surah.

Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, concerning ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾, he said: The Muslims said at Uhud [i.e., their previous statement: "If we gain the upper hand..." etc.]. Then He said ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ ... to His saying ﴿it is indeed better for the patient﴾, and then after it ﴿But be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah﴾.

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: When the mutilation befell the people of Uhud, the Muslims said: "If we gain the upper hand over them, we will certainly mutilate them." So Allah said: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient﴾. Then He resolved and informed that one should not mutilate, so He forbade mutilation. He said: The unbelievers mutilated the slain of Uhud, except Hanzala ibn al-Rahib; Abu ʿAmir al-Rahib was with Abu Sufyan, so they left Hanzala because of that.

Others said: That was abrogated by His saying in Bara'a: ﴿Kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾. They said: He said ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾ as a report from Allah to the believers that they should not begin fighting with them until they begin with it. He said: ﴿And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you, and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not love the transgressors﴾.

Mention of those who said this:

Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾, he said: This is a report from Allah to His Prophet that he should fight whoever fights him. He said: Then Bara'a was revealed, and the sacred months ended. He said: So this is among the abrogated.

Others said: Allah, may He be exalted, meant by His saying ﴿But be patient, and your patience is not except through Allah﴾ only the Prophet of Allah, to the exclusion of the rest of his Companions, so the command to be patient was a resolve from Allah for him alone, not for them.

Mention of those who said this:

Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾: He said: Allah commanded them to pardon the polytheists. Then men among them who had strength embraced Islam and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if Allah had permitted us, we would have avenged ourselves on these dogs." So the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished. But if you are patient, it is indeed better for the patient﴾, and "Be patient, O Muhammad, and do not be in distress over those who take revenge; and your patience is not except through Allah." Then this was abrogated, and He commanded them to fight them. So all of this is abrogated.

Others said: These two verses did not mean anything of what those mentioned; rather, they meant that whoever is wronged with an injustice may not inflict on his wrongdoer more than what the wrongdoer inflicted on him. They said: the verse is definitive (muhkam), not abrogated.

Mention of those who said this:

Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Khalid, from Ibn Sirin, concerning ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾, he said: If a man takes something from you, take from him its like.

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: If he takes something from you, take from him its like. Al-Hasan said: ʿAbd al-Razzaq said: Sufyan said: They say: If he takes a dinar from you, do not take from him except a dinar, and if he takes something from you, do not take from him except the like of that thing.

Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us; and al-Harith narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: Warqa' narrated to us, all from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning ﴿And if you punish, then punish with the like of that with which you were punished﴾: "do not transgress."

Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, the like of it.

The correct view on this matter is to say: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded whoever among the believers is wronged with an injury to inflict upon whoever wronged him the like of what was done to him, if he chooses to take that punishment; and He informed him that patience in refraining from punishment, for what was done to him, is better; and He resolved upon His Prophet ﷺ to be patient. This is because that is the apparent meaning of the revelation, and the interpretations we have mentioned from those who transmitted them are all possible readings of the whole verse. Since that is the case, and there is no indication in the verse, either by report or by reason, as to which of these was intended, it is obligatory upon us to apply the ruling of the verse generally, not to restrict its interpretation to a particular meaning for which there is no indication... and to say: it is a definitive verse, by which Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, commanded His servants not to transgress in what is due to them from others, whether property or life, beyond the right which Allah has left to them to pursue through another; and that it is not abrogated, since there is no indication of its abrogation; and that the view that it is definitive has a correct and understandable basis.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 127:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Be patient, and your patience is only through God. And do not grieve over them, and do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ (16:127).

God, mentioned and exalted is He, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Be patient, O Muhammad, over what harm has befallen you for the sake of God. ﴿And your patience is only through God﴾ means: and your patience, if you are patient, is only by the help of God and His granting you success in that. ﴿And do not grieve over them﴾ means: do not grieve over these polytheists who deny you and reject what you have brought, who turn away from you and disregard the admonition I have brought them. ﴿And do not be in distress because of what they plot﴾ means: let not your breast be constricted by what they say out of ignorance, and by their attributing what you have brought to sorcery, poetry, or soothsaying. "What they plot" means: what they devise through deceptive schemes in barring from the way of God those who wish to believe in you and to affirm what God has sent down to you.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of this. The majority of the readers of Iraq recited ﴿and do not be in distress [ḍayq]﴾ with a fatḥah on the ḍād in ḍayq, according to the meaning I have described in its interpretation. Some of the readers of Medina recited ﴿and do not be in distress [ḍīq]﴾ with a kasrah on the ḍād.

The more correct of the two recitations in our view is the recitation of the one who reads ḍayq with a fatḥah on the ḍād, because God, exalted is He, only forbade His Prophet (ﷺ) from having his breast constricted by the harm he met from the polytheists in conveying to them the revelation and sending down of God. He said to him: ﴿So let there be no discomfort in your breast from it, that you may warn thereby﴾ [7:2], and He said: ﴿Perhaps you would leave some of what is revealed to you, and your breast would be constricted by it because they say, "Why has not a treasure been sent down to him or an angel come with him?" You are only a warner﴾ [11:12]. Since this was what God, mentioned and exalted is He, had forbidden him, the fatḥah on the ḍād is the familiar usage of the Arabs for that meaning. The Arabs say: "In my breast there is ḍayq (constriction) regarding this matter." The ḍād is pronounced with a kasrah for things that are lived in, such as ḍīq (narrowness) of a dwelling and the like. If ḍayq with a fatḥah occurs in a place where ḍīq with a kasrah would be expected, that is for something that is sometimes spacious and sometimes narrow, from a lack of ease, and it has two possible explanations: either it is the plural of ḍayqah, as the poet A'sha of Banu Tha'labah said:

"Then surely your Lord, out of His mercy, has removed the ḍayqah from us and widened [us]..."

[The verse is in the Diwan of A'sha Banu Tha'labah, Maymun ibn Qays (Cairo edition, p. 237), from a qasidah in praise of Iyas ibn Qabisah al-Ta'i, and it is the fourth in the poem. In (Lisan al-Arab: ḍ-y-q): ḍayq: doubt that arises in the heart. From God's saying (and do not be in distress because of what they plot): al-Farra' said: ḍayq is what your breast cannot contain. And ḍīq (with kasrah) is what is found in something that widens and narrows, like a house or a garment. When you see ḍayq (with fatḥah) in place of ḍīq (with kasrah), it is due to one of two matters: first, that it is the plural of ḍayqah, as A'sha said: "Then surely your Lord..." the verse. The other: that it refers to something narrow, so ḍayq is a lightened form whose original is with the shaddah, like hayn and layn.]

Or it is the lightened form of the narrow thing, as the lightened form of hayyin layyin is used, so one says: "He is hayn layn (easy and gentle)."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 16, verse 128:

The interpretation of His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good (ihsan).﴾

His, the Exalted's, saying means: O Muhammad, ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ ﴿is with those who fear Him﴾, that is, those who fear Allah regarding His prohibitions, so they avoid them and fear His punishment for them, and so they refrain from transgressing them. ﴿And those who are doers of good﴾ means: He is with those who perfect the observance of His obligations, the upholding of His rights, and the constant obedience to Him in what He has commanded them and forbidden them.

And in accordance with what we have said on this matter, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan: ﴿Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him and those who are doers of good﴾. He said: "Fear Allah regarding what He has forbidden them, and do good in what He has made obligatory upon them."

Al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: It was mentioned to us that Harim ibn Hayyan al-'Abdi, when death came upon him, was told: "Make a bequest." He said: "I do not know what to bequeath, but sell my coat of mail and settle my debt for me. If it is not sufficient, then sell my horse. If that is not sufficient, then sell my servant. And I charge you with the final verses of Surat al-Nahl: ﴿Call to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good admonition, and argue with them in the best manner. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided. And if you punish, then punish with the like of what you were punished with. But if you are patient, it is better for the patient.﴾" It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when this verse was revealed, said: "Rather, we will be patient."

End of Surat al-Nahl
